**Planner ruling 3A-1 (Fable, 11:58 AST): lifecycle request builder authorized.** The writer found no accepted function that
builds a register/unregister request from a saved workflow (`expectedEpoch` / `registrationEpoch` / `expectedRevision` have
no recorded source). Narrow addition to the pinned `lib/cloudWorkflowRegistration.ts` (+ tests) is authorized: a PURE
`lifecycleRequestFor(kind, regs, authority, { id, revision }, digest)` that never throws and returns the typed request or a
typed refusal. Rule: the record for `registrationKey(authority, id)`; an intent in `pending|dispatching|uncertain|divergent`
⇒ `unresolved` (Recover first); the lifecycle proof is `registrationIn(record.last.answer)` (the pinned parser; a typed
refusal never folds into `last`, so `last` is a proof or null). register: no record/no proof ⇒ `expectedEpoch 0`;
proof `unregistered` ⇒ `expectedEpoch = proof.registrationEpoch`; proof `active` ⇒ refuse `active` (an `update` for a
changed revision is a later packet). unregister: proof `active` ⇒ `{ registrationEpoch: proof.registrationEpoch,
expectedRevision: proof.revision }` with `proof.workflowDigest` as the digest for `prepareIntent`; otherwise refuse
`inactive`. Matches the Worker CAS rule (`cloudWorkflowProtocol.ts` `conflictOk`: null row needs 0, unregistered row needs
its epoch). Digest for register = `workflowDigestOf(workflow)` (`lib/cloudWorkflowCapture.ts`). Existing assertions untouched.

#### DT-7C-3D fix round (Sonnet 5.5, 22 Oct 2026) - planner review 3D, ACCEPT WITH ONE FIX

**Status: DONE.**

- **Fix (concern 3).** `deliverableOf` cannot tell an acknowledged proof apart (the stored receipt's `ackedVersion` only moves on Check
  status), and `DeliverableView` carries no version, so the Cloud results card keeps an `acked` map (proof key -> stored receipt version at
  the ack) in component state. The stored version comes from the pinned `readReconciliation` on `useStore(s => s.cloudReconciliation)`
  (a read of an existing selector; hub, store, controllers untouched). Confirm delivery is disabled while `acked[key] === current version`;
  the handler also returns early for an acked key. Set only for `kind: "answered"` with `parsed.outcome === "ok"` (refused, unconfirmed,
  stale and Worker-refused answers never disable it). A proof that leaves the deliverable list forgets its entry (state adjusted during
  render, not in an effect: the React lint rule forbids setState in an effect); a newer stored receipt version re-enables it. The
  "The Worker noted it" status line is unchanged. No message key added.
- **Tests.** `WorkflowCloud.test.tsx`: new test "two clicks send one ack, disabled once acknowledged, enabled again when the proof changes
  version" (two clicks -> one `ack`; disabled; same version re-read and a forced click still one; version 3 -> 4 enables and a click
  makes the second `ack`; gone then re-listed at the same version is confirmable; an unconfirmed ack never disables). One existing assertion
  changed on purpose: in "Confirm delivery: one ack(key) per row..." row 0 was asserted enabled after its acknowledged ack; it is now asserted
  disabled (row 1 busy-disabled assertion unchanged). The test file mocks `readReconciliation` through a pass-through wrapper that fakes the
  stored versions only while `fake.s.versions` is set (after the screen is up: the store parses that slice itself on every save), reset in
  `beforeEach`. `e2e/workflow-cloud.spec.ts` case g: after the first acknowledged ack the button is disabled, a forced second click leaves
  exactly one `ack` in the Worker log (before: two, the second answered idempotently), Check status then still retires the proof.

### DT-7C-3B record (Opus 5.5, 22 Oct 2026)

**Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS (12:40 AST).** The design below was recorded before any code edit; the results are at the end.

- **Component tree.** New `components/social/workflows/WorkflowCloud.tsx` holds the shared pieces: `useCloudView()`
  (`useSyncExternalStore` over `cloudHub().subscribe`, re-subscribing on `pageshow`, a constant unconfigured view as
  the server snapshot), `CloudConnect` (connection line + **Check connection**), the copy helpers, `WorkflowCloudCard`
  and `CloudResultsCard`. `WorkflowsScreen` renders `CloudResultsCard` in the list view and calls `leaveCloudScreen()`
  on unmount (one effect at the top, so list and editor switches never leave). `WorkflowEditor` renders
  `WorkflowCloudCard` after the local run history and routes **Run now**. `ArticleEditor` routes **Mark ready**. Every
  action calls `cloudHub()` at click time; no hub object is kept in state or refs.
- **Hub calls per button (exactly one each, nothing chained, nothing at mount):**
  - Check connection → `cloudHub().handshake()` (busy key `handshake`).
  - Put on cloud / Take off cloud / Recover → `register(id)` / `unregister(id)` / `recover(id)` (busy key `wf:<id>`).
  - Entry Send / Check status / Run / Cancel → `submit(key)` / `status(key)` / `run(key)` / `cancel(key)` (busy key =
    the journal entry key).
  - Fetch results → `reconcile({ limit: CHANGES_LIMIT_MAX })` (50, imported, busy key `reconcile`).
  - Confirm delivery → `ack(key)` (busy key = the proof key).
  - Run now: `cloudHub().captureAuthority(id)` non-null → `captureManualRun(id, { authority, articleId? })`; null →
    today's `runWorkflowNow` expression unchanged.
  - All lifecycle/occurrence/ack/reconcile buttons are disabled while their busy key is set or while
    `view().authority` is null (then the card shows "connect in Settings" or **Check connection**).
- **State chip (first match wins):** (1) id fails `WF_ID_RE` (imported from the Worker protocol) → `unsupported id`.
  (2) own record = the `registrations()` row for this id whose origin equals the configured origin and, once
  handshaken, whose ownerKey equals `view().authority.ownerKey`: intent `pending|dispatching|uncertain|divergent` →
  `unresolved` (Recover shown); intent `refused` → `refused` (the Worker's `lastRefusal` as copy); `proof === "active"`
  and paused → `paused on cloud`; `proof === "active"` → `on cloud`; otherwise `local`. (3) any other row for this id →
  `another Worker` (no buttons). (4) no row and `counts().registrations >= REGISTRATION_CAPACITY` → `capacity` (Put on
  cloud disabled). (5) `local`.
- **Selector added to the hub (read-only):** `deliverable()` = `deliverableOf(readReconciliation(slice))`: proofs whose
  stored receipt is terminal, has no collision output, is not retired (tombstone) and has `ackedVersion <
  receiptVersion`. This is the Confirm delivery list. Test added to `lib/cloudWorkflowHub.test.ts`.
- **Mark ready:** for each stored workflow with trigger `article-ready` whose `registrations()` row has `proof ===
  "active"`, take `cloudHub().captureAuthority(w.id)`; the first non-null authority routes the click to
  `captureArticleReady(articleId, { authority })` (ready/unchanged settle like a success; refusals map to copy;
  save-type refusals reuse the editor's existing handling). No such authority → the existing
  `act(() => useStore.getState().setArticleStatus(id, "ready"))` unchanged.
- **New message keys:** `workflows.cloud.*` in `messages/workflows.{ar,en}.json` (title, chips, buttons, connection,
  handshake, intent states, reason table, capture refusals, entries, runs, results, delivery, pauses) and
  `website.cloudReady.*` in `messages/website.{ar,en}.json` (Mark-ready refusals + captured note). Final list below.
- **Result: message keys (ar = en, 144 + 21).** `workflows.cloud.`: `title`, `note`, `chip.{local,active,paused,another,
  unresolved,refused,unsupported,capacity}`, `anotherHelp`, `unsupportedHelp`, `capacityHelp`, `refusedHelp`, `put`,
  `takeOff`, `recover`, `connect.{none,bad,origin,settings,need}`, `check`, `handshake.{busy,ok,refused,uncertain}`,
  `intent.{settled,refused,uncertain,dispatching,pending,divergent}`, `sent`, `notSent`, `notSaved`, `answered`,
  `answeredOk`, `workerRefused`, `invalidAnswer`, `reason.*` (one table for every controller/session/hub/Worker code,
  with "-" normalized to "_", plus `reason.other` "{reason}" for any unknown code), `capture.<CaptureRefusalReason>` (all
  22, statically checked by a template-literal key type), `captured`, `entries`, `entry.{queued,suppressed,observed,none,
  rejected}`, `send`, `status`, `run`, `cancel`, `runs`, `state.{pending,running,done,partial,failed,cancelled}`,
  `results.{title,fetch,page,more,blocked,empty}`, `deliver.{title,help,button,done}`, `proofFull`, `retirementFull`.
  `website.cloudReady.<reason>` for the 20 capture refusals other than `not-persisted` / `unsupported-save` (those keep
  the editor's existing save-error handling), plus `website.cloudReady.captured` "{count}". Limits in copy come from the
  code: `REGISTRATION_CAPACITY`, `PROOF_CAPACITY`, `TOMBSTONES_MAX`, `CHANGES_LIMIT_MAX`. No size limit is retyped (the
  too-large copy names no number; 3C owns the limits sentence).
- **Result: Mark ready.** A cloud `ready`/`unchanged` settles as a success (count of captured cloud runs shown). A
  refusal shows its `website.cloudReady.*` copy and returns `{ok:false, reason:"issues"}` to `settle()`, which adds

  `lib/cloudWorkflowRegistration.ts` (inserted before the persistence-contract section). It is pure and wrapped in
  try/catch. An invalid key, revision (`isVersion`) or digest (`DIGEST_RE`) gives `invalid`. An intent in
  `pending|dispatching|uncertain|divergent` gives `unresolved`. The proof is `registrationIn(record.last.answer)`.
  register: no proof gives `expectedEpoch 0`, `unregistered` gives its epoch, `active` refuses `active`. unregister:
  `active` binds `{registrationEpoch, expectedRevision: proof.revision}` with the proof's digest; anything else is
  `inactive`. 5 new tests in `lib/cloudWorkflowRegistration.test.ts` (appended; one import line added; zero existing
  lines changed): each branch, `prepareIntent` round trips for both kinds, and register → unregister → re-register at
  `expectedEpoch = 1`.
- **Hub API (`lib/cloudWorkflowHub.ts`):** `cloudHub()` is a lazy singleton built by `createCloudHub(deps)`. deps =
  the three controllers, `readRegistrations()`, `onDispose?`. Without `window` it is an inert hub: actions refuse
  `no-browser`. View: `CloudHubView {configured, authority, handshake, busy, last}`, plus `view()` and `subscribe(cb)`.
  Actions: `handshake()` (the three controllers in turn; returns the registration result), `register/unregister/
  recover(workflowId)` (busy/last key `wf:<id>`), `submit/status/run/cancel(key)`, `check/ack(key)`
  (key = occurrence key), `reconcile(opts?)` (key `reconcile`). Selectors: `authorityFor(workflowId)`,
  `captureAuthority(workflowId)`, `registrations()`, `counts()`, `cloudRuns()`. Teardown: `leave()`, `dispose()`, and
  the exported `leaveCloudScreen()`.
- **Name and shape changes from the plan sketch, and why:**
  - `configured.reason` also allows `"disposed"`, from `ConfigureResult`.
  - `RegistrationView` adds `key`, `proof` (`active|unregistered|null`) and `paused` next to `state` (the intent
    state), so 3B can draw its chips without re-parsing.
  - `counts()` values are `number | null` (null = that slice is unreadable). `journal` reuses the store's
    `cloudJournalRetained`.
  - Added `leave()`: `leaveCloudScreen()` calls `invalidateCloudVisit()` and then, only if a hub exists, `leave()`.
    It invalidates every controller visit and clears the view authority. The registration controller does not read
    the store fence, so otherwise it would keep its authority across visits.
  - `pagehide` also calls `invalidateCloudVisit()` (plan rule 4) before `dispose()`. `dispose` resets the singleton,
    so a bfcache return builds a fresh hub.
- **register/unregister:** the authority comes from the view (none → `no_authority`). The workflow comes from
  `useStore` `workflows` (missing → `missing`). Then `readRegistrations()`, i.e. `cloudRegistrationPersistence.read`,
  which re-verifies (null → `unreadable`). Then `workflowDigestOf(workflow)` (null → `""` → `invalid`), then
  `lifecycleRequestFor`. A refusal is returned as `{kind:"refused", reason, dispatched:false}` with no controller call.
  Otherwise exactly one `register(request)` or `unregister(request, digest)`. recover sends
  `registrationKey(authority, id)`.
- **Fences:** the hub adds no request fence. The controllers keep cfg/visit/auth/latest/disposed, and Occ/Recon also
  read `cloudFence()`. A hub-local generation (bumped on configure/leave/dispose) only stops an older handshake from
  writing its authority into the view. Busy counts per key, so two concurrent actions on one key cannot clear each
  other's busy mark.

Design recorded before code (the writer records exact schema/field names, the import/retirement transition table and any
refinement in its record BEFORE editing):

1. **7C2C-1 — ownership survives retirement.** A retirement tombstone keeps compact ownership for every output the proof
   owned (output id, kind, action, adopted-bytes digest, disposition), not only already-deleted ones; full receipt bodies are
   still dropped. Deletion capture (`applyDeletions` and every idea/post/plan removal path, ordinary queued removal and
   reset/import removal) consults live proofs AND tombstones, marking a removed tombstone-owned id `deleted` atomically with
   the durable removal. Import treats tombstone-owned `deleted` ids exactly like live-proof deletion evidence (never
   restored). Still-present retired outputs stay untouched (dirty drafts are never deleted because their proof retired);
   foreign/unowned collision rules unchanged.
2. **7C2C-2 — no silent loss of anti-resurrection evidence.** No oldest-first eviction. Preferred bounded design: when the
   tombstone bound is reached, the oldest tombstones fold into a compact verifiable per-authority retirement watermark
   (monotonic, merged by max on import) derived from an ordering the stored proof and an imported proof both carry
   (writer verifies which field — e.g. the authority's server change sequence or receipt version — gives a sound total order
   for retired versus newer work); any imported or held proof at or below the watermark for that authority that is not live
   locally is refused as retired, with its outputs not restored. Where the order cannot prove newer work it fails closed
   (refuse with a typed reason; recovery is an explicit fresh status from the Worker, never automatic network revalidation
   during import). If no sound order exists, the fallback is refuse-at-bound: retirement past the bound returns a typed
   `retirement-full` refusal (proof stays live, counting toward 600 with the existing `proof-full` result) and an import
   whose union would exceed the bound refuses — the writer records why and the recovery path. Either way: old and new backup
   formats documented, a backup/held receipt/reload cannot bypass the bound, truthful capacity/refusal results.
3. **7C2C-3 — reset applies to imported first proof.** Before the existing atomic restore commit, each incoming cloud proof
   (including one with no local proof) and its associated outputs is rechecked against the fresh merged journal suppression
   (max epoch/`resetAt`) using its exact bound identity/executionAt. Pre-reset work yields a suppressed disposition and no
   restored outputs; unrelated ordinary drafts and genuinely post-reset cloud work are unaffected; already-owned dirty local
   outputs follow the existing contract. Deletion unions, current durable validation, read-back/rollback and "no fabricated
   ack authority" stay.

Rules recorded before editing (writer refines the full transition table in its record BEFORE coding):
1. **Key / record.** Key = canonical origin + server ownerKey + workflowId. Record = immutable intent (exact validated
   register/unregister request + descriptor body, workflow revision/digest, local operation/commit id, created time) +
   attempt reservations + observed bound results + per-key epoch/revision history. No credential or token fingerprint.
   One unresolved lifecycle intent per key.
2. **States (minimum):** `pending` (persisted, not yet dispatched) → `dispatching` (attempt reserved durably) → one of
   `settled` (definitive bound success via exact CAS/read-back), `uncertain` (dispatched; stale/timeout/receipt_unavailable/
   lost answer), `refused` (typed refusal for that attempt — never proof an earlier uncertain attempt did not apply, so a
   prior uncertainty stays), `divergent` (conflict / contradiction; blocks automatic resolution). Recovery
   (`uncertain`/`dispatching`-after-reload → `dispatching`) only by explicit call, new matching handshake and a fresh
   durable attempt reservation, replaying the **identical** saved request; no new epoch/revision/digest/body; no parallel
   recovery per key; never automatic on construction/reload/hydration/import/reset/network error.
3. **Persistence.** Inside `3z-prod-articles`: fresh durable read, CAS, write, exact read-back, THEN dispatch. Failed/
   unsupported/unreadable persistence ⇒ zero mutation requests. No new storage key or lock. The new slice is added to the
   locked-only ordinary-save set (verbatim from fresh storage).
4. **Controller fences.** Owns configure/visit lifecycle through the accepted session; requires a validated matching
   handshake; captures detached plain data before any await (no new reentrant abort callback that launches session
   actions; throwing accessors are not a supported input); config/token/visit/latest-action/A-B-A/original-authority/
   operation-identity fences across every await, persistence and request; never retargets a saved intent; stale
   completions recorded only as observations bound to their original intent.
5. **Validation.** Saved request/response JSON re-parsed through the pinned protocol (incl. `Parsed.authority` and request
   binding) on load/import; no trust in serialized brands; epoch/revision history never regresses or mixes authorities.
6. **Reset / deletion / import / projections.** Reset keeps lifecycle evidence and unresolved recovery; workflow deletion
   neither erases it nor unregisters remotely; import revalidates and monotonically merges under the same lock/read-back,
   preserves local unresolved work, rejects immutable identity/intent contradictions; older backups cannot resurrect
   settled decisions; legacy backups without the slice keep it; public/shared projections exclude it; cap 100 keys
   (refuse new, no eviction; existing-key recovery still allowed).

byte-identical.

**API (names fixed for this packet):** `createCloudWorkflowSession({ fetch })` returns
`{ configure({ origin, token }), invalidateVisit(), dispose(), handshake(), execute(request) }`.
- `configure`: canonicalizes the origin with the protocol helper; any actual change of origin or token clears authority
  and increments `configGen`; an identical value is a no-op.
- `invalidateVisit`: increments `visitGen` (even when returning to the same visible target) and clears authority.
- `dispose`: permanent; every outstanding and later call resolves as stale/refused with zero new fetches.
- `handshake()`: `describeRequest({kind:'authority'})`, one fetch, `parseAnswer` at the captured canonical origin; only a
  valid answer installs authority (origin + server ownerKey) for the current config/visit generation, and only if it is
  still the latest action.
- `execute(request)`: supported kinds authority/register/update/pause/resume/unregister/submit/status/run/cancel only;
  `ack`/`changes` excluded in the TypeScript type and refused at runtime with zero fetch. Requires the request's
  intended Authority and ownerKey (submit: body ownerKey) to equal the current handshake's; otherwise zero fetch, never
  retargeted. No arbitrary URL/method/header API.
- Result union: `{ kind: 'refused', reason }` (pre-dispatch, zero fetch) | `{ kind: 'answer', parsed, binding, meta }`
  (complete parser result incl. `Parsed.authority`, detached request binding, nonsecret meta incl. `dispatched`) |
  `{ kind: 'uncertain', category, authority, binding, meta }` (dispatched network/timeout/abort/redirect/oversize/
  malformed/mixed/receipt_unavailable after a POST) | `{ kind: 'stale', dispatched, authority, binding, meta }`
  (completion after a fence). Typed `Parsed.refused` answers are returned unchanged with dispatch metadata and never
  labelled safe-to-retry.

**Session rules:** capture synchronously before the first await: detached request + nested expectations (reuse
`detachRequest`, which keeps the protocol's optional-undefined behaviour; no naive JSON clone), canonical origin, token,
`configGen`, `visitGen`, current authority, and a per-action sequence number from a monotonic counter (latest-action
fence). Recheck the fence after every await, immediately before fetch, during streaming, after parse/digest validation
and before returning; a superseded action returns `stale` and cannot install authority or release another action's
state. Destination = captured origin + pinned descriptor path; headers `Authorization: Bearer <token>` +
`Content-Type`; `credentials: 'omit'`, `cache: 'no-store'`, `redirect: 'manual'`; redirects and an unexpected final
response URL refused (uncertain after POST). Exact serialized UTF-8 request checked against REQUEST_BYTES_MAX 32,768
before fetch. Response read by bounded streaming with `RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX = 1 MiB` (cancel on overflow; Content-Length
not trusted) and `DEADLINE_MS = 15000` across network + body; JSON parsed only after complete receipt; no
`response.json()`/`text()` unbounded. Token never in results, errors, logs, keys or fixtures. No retry, replay,
implicit handshake or fallback host. Registration uncertainty is reported only (no repeated mutations, no Worker
change). Prove a maximum-supported full receipt fits 1 MiB, or stop and record the discrepancy.

Approach ruling (before edits; the writer records the full inventory first):
1. **Field-ownership inventory** of every `pickLocal` field: exclusively locked (changed only inside
   `3z-prod-articles` transactions — e.g. `cloudJournal`, and whichever of `articles`, Ready/workflow runs, Inbox
   send/control op slices the code shows are locked-only), ordinary (settings and other plain `set` paths), and mixed
   (both). Derived from the code's actual write sites, not assumed. Recorded as a table in the writer's record before any
   code edit.
2. **Three-way merge at save time, inside the lock.** The queued ordinary save keeps a per-tab **base** = the durable
   state this tab last knew (set on hydration, after each own successful write, after each own locked commit's read-back,
   and on storage/rehydrate events). At execution, for each field: exclusively-locked → fresh durable value verbatim;
   ours == base → fresh durable value (this tab did not change it); fresh == base → ours; both changed → for keyed record
   collections, a per-id three-way merge (apply only this tab's own adds/updates/deletes relative to base onto fresh, so
   another tab's locked adds/updates/deletes are kept and nothing is resurrected), and for plain ordinary scalars the
   existing last-writer-wins (ours). Mixed slices keep both legitimate changes and their existing contract; if a mixed
   slice cannot be merged without changing its contract, stop and record the concrete boundary.
3. **Same-tab ordering.** A pending ordinary save that runs after a same-tab locked action must not replay obsolete
   contents: the locked action updates the base (and memory) to its read-back, so the later save diffs against it.
4. Journal bytes stay verbatim; unreadable-storage refusal, shared Web Lock serialization, coalescing, immediate UI,
   no recursive locking, no unlocked fallback, import/reset CAS + durable rollback, Inbox merge, local workflow and Ready
   atomicity unchanged. No new storage key or schema migration; if one is required, stop and record it.
5. Silent-setItem-drop: non-blocking observation; optional cheap truthful read-back only if it never clobbers newer
   durable data; the original diagnostic result is preserved, not relabelled.

Rulings (before edits):
1. **7C2A-1 design (single key, serialized writers).** Keep the one existing storage key and the existing
   `3z-prod-articles` lock; no second key, schema or persistence mechanism. Ordinary saves never author journal bytes:
   the persist storage adapter's write becomes a coalesced, serialized task that, **inside the lock**, reads the fresh
   durable payload, takes its journal bytes verbatim (and any slice only locked paths own), and writes them together with
   the **latest** in-memory ordinary fields at execution time (not a snapshot captured at enqueue; multiple queued saves
   collapse to one). Locked journal commits/reset/import keep their own exact write + read-back. Rollback paths build
   from durable state read under the lock. No recursive acquisition: a save triggered inside a locked callback is queued
   and runs after release; nothing awaits the lock from inside it. In-memory UI updates stay immediate. Without Web
   Locks (no tab can lock-commit a journal), an ordinary save may write synchronously while preserving the stored
   journal bytes verbatim; it never writes in-memory journal bytes. Disclose the residual: a queued ordinary save can be
   lost if the tab closes before the lock is granted. If this design proves infeasible inside `store/index.ts`, stop and
   record the concrete alternative before editing (contract item 1).
2. **7C2A-2.** Distinguish: no value; valid envelope without journal (legacy, supported); malformed whole JSON;
   invalid outer shape (`null`, array, missing/non-object `state`); malformed nested journal. Any read failure (thrown
   getItem, parse failure, invalid shape) makes the save/commit/reset/import refuse without writing, preserving the
   bytes, with a typed, observable failure (journal actions return it; ordinary saves expose a store-level persistence
   status that Settings can show, no new UI beyond honest failure copy if required). No automatic overwrite/recovery;
   the old ordinary-save repair assertion changes with its exact reason recorded before the edit.
3. **7C2A-3.** Observation identity = authority + occurrence + body digest + canonical full receipt; request kind
   (Submit/Run/Cancel/Status) is not part of the conflict key. Identical receipts are idempotent; keep the first stored
   provenance (deterministic). Monotonic versions and ack enrichment kept; real equal-version contradictions, foreign
   authority/digest/identity, forged/compact proof still refused; import revalidates through the pinned parser.
4. **7C2A-4.** Restore rollback is built from the durable pre-restore payload read under the shared lock; a failed
   write/read-back reconciles to newer durable truth (never clobbers another tab's newer ordinary fields) and returns
   `not-persisted`; for legacy and journal-bearing backups; Inbox-control merge, journal union/conflict/cap, Settings'
   awaited result and no candidate-library replacement on failure preserved; positive reset rollback kept.
5. **Writable** exactly the contract list: `lib/cloudWorkflowJournal.ts` (+ test), journal storage/import/reset parts of
   `store/index.ts`, `store/cloudWorkflows.test.ts`, narrowly related `store/index.test.ts` regressions, Settings
   failure/result handling + test only if required, EN/AR Settings copy and `e2e/settings.spec.ts` if needed, tool 38,
   appended design contract/test-matrix notes, this handoff (record). Any change to an existing assertion is listed with
   its reason in the record BEFORE it is made; no blanket weakening.
6. **Probe and browser hygiene.** Before the first run of any copied Codex probe: copy into
   `%TEMP%/claude-dt7c2ar1-writer/probes/` and redirect every output/cache/report/afterAll/screenshot path, including
   `PWTEST_CACHE_DIR`, Playwright `outputDir`/reporters and vitest cache; hash the whole Codex evidence tree before and
   after. Browser fault/regression tests use isolated profiles with external requests blocked (route-abort non-localhost),
   never the configured real profile or a normal Settings tab that auto-pulls Worker status; never reset/import real
   Chrome storage; no screenshots/logs with credentials.

Checks: reproduce each finding RED on the frozen source; bounded regressions with positive controls per contract
"Required evidence"; focused tests; after final changes the full app suite once (Worker excluded), app typecheck, lint,
changed-file Prettier, `pnpm build` (existing :3000 server, no restart, no new port), scoped settings/workflows/website

Rulings (before edits):
1. **Files.** New `lib/cloudWorkflowJournal.ts` (+ `.test.ts`), new `store/cloudWorkflows.test.ts`; additive journal
   schema/defaults/projection/actions plus the narrowly necessary reset/import durability in `store/index.ts` (+ existing

2. **Reuse the existing durability mechanism.** Journal writes go through the store's existing shared Web Lock
   `3z-prod-articles` commit/read-back path (fresh durable read under the lock, CAS on generation/base, exact read-back
   of generation, affected commit and immutable identity/digest/version); no parallel lock or storage layer, no network
   under the lock, typed failures (missing Web Locks, blocked/quota storage, malformed stored journal, failed read-back)
   and never an empty-journal fallback over unreadable data. Rollback never clobbers newer durable state.
3. **Keys/entries.** Canonical structured `(origin, ownerKey, occurrenceId)` key from the accepted protocol helpers; entry
   keeps original authority, immutable allowlisted body/digest, captured executionAt, local commit token, typed local
   state. Same key + digest idempotent; changed digest conflicts without replacement; authorities never merge/retarget;
   no transfer to the local executor; no bearer/fingerprint/private/unrelated data.

   versions never replace newer; equal-version contradictions conflict; no ackable/delivered marking. If the pinned
   protocol cannot revalidate a stored receipt without editing it, stop and return NEEDS_CONTEXT.
5. **Cap/suppression/import/reset** exactly as contract items 4–6: cap 600 (update at cap, refuse new, overflowing import
   fails before write, no eviction); monotonic `{epoch, resetAt, commitId}` advanced by reset under the lock and proven;
   suppression by immutable executionAt; import merges against fresh durable journal (unresolved entries kept, monotonic
   receipts, original authorities, max epoch and max resetAt independently incl. equal-counter branches, contradictions
   reported, legacy backup keeps current journal, Inbox-control restore merge/read-back preserved). Reset awaitable with
   explicit result; no synchronous bypass that can erase the journal.
6. **Settings.** Read the installed Next.js guides first. Reset waits, busy guard prevents double confirm, failure never

2. **Fixture chronology.** Any maintained fixture whose `executionAt` precedes its registration's `opened_at` is moved to a
   chronologically valid instant with an inline `// DT-7B-R1 fixture correction (chronology): …` comment naming the
   original value; its behavioral assertions stay identical. Every corrected fixture is listed in the record with the
   original and new instant. Copied Codex probes run unmodified first; if a probe's own fixture conflicts with the exact
   chronology, adapt only the scratch copy, labelled, with the original result preserved next to it.
3. **Full receipt proof (7B-2).** The route validates a status/submit/cancel receipt by re-running the shared admission
   validator on the stored body with `nowMs = Date.parse(receipt.createdAt)` (admission time, so historical bodies stay
   valid), recomputing the canonical payload digest with the shared protocol helper and comparing it to
   `payloadDigest`, and binding `ownerKey`/`occurrenceId`/`workflowId`/`kind`/`registrationEpoch`/`revision` to the body.
   The state/step/output proof table mirrors the coordinator's actual transitions (writer derives it from
   `workflowCoordinator.ts` and records it): pending = all steps pending, no `startedAt`/`finishedAt`, no outputs;
   running = `startedAt`, a resolved prefix then a pending suffix, or a fully resolved list before finish; done = all
   done; partial = ≥1 done then the fail-fast failed step and skipped rest; failed = no done step, failed then skipped;
   cancelled = all skipped, no outputs, no `startedAt`. Each step status requires/forbids its fields (done:
   output id/digest; failed: an allowed error incl. `output-conflict`; pending/skipped: neither). Outputs: one per done
   step, `wf:<occurrenceId>:<actionId>` ids, action/kind match, exact allowlisted draft shape, canonical record digest
   recomputed and equal; unknown keys anywhere fail. Legitimate acknowledged receipts, historical timestamps,
   running-before-finish and partial shapes stay readable.
4. **Feed proof.** The compact wire shape and the exact `nextAfter`/`more` rule stay. Each item: unique `occurrenceId` in
   the page, bounded step count (≤ the protocol action cap), contiguous unique `idx` from 0, unique action ids, allowed
   kinds, the same per-state step table as ruling 3, outputs only on terminal items with the same output checks and
   recomputed record digests, linked to their done steps. The feed has no body, so it proves no body/target binding; full
   status stays the authority for later reconciliation (documented, not claimed).
5. **Mutation binding.** Success answers are bound to the request using the coordinator's real semantics (writer reads
   them from the code and captures real control answers): register `created:true|false` ⇒ the requested workflow, epoch
   `expectedEpoch + 1`, requested revision and digest, registered; update ⇒ requested epoch, revision and digest, with
   `changed` consistent with `expectedRevision`; pause/resume ⇒ requested epoch, the expected revision and the requested
   paused flag; unregister ⇒ requested epoch closed at the expected revision. Cancel: `cancelled:true` ⇒ a valid
   cancelled receipt; `cancelled:false` ⇒ a valid receipt in a terminal state the coordinator leaves unchanged. Ack:
   versions and `firstAckAt` mutually consistent (`ackedVersion ≤ receiptVersion`, `firstAckAt` iff `ackedVersion ≥ 1`),
   exact-terminal acknowledgement and legitimate stale no-ops kept. A plausible answer for the same workflow that does not
   match the request is `503 receipt_unavailable`. Where the real coordinator semantics differ from this summary, the
   code wins and the writer records the difference.
6. **Refusals.** A per-operation allowed-error table (derived from what each coordinator op can return) plus typed,
   range-checked extras: ids equal to the request, `payloadDigest` a digest, `prunedAt` ISO, `state` in the state set,
   `receiptVersion` a version, `registration` null or a valid registration bound to the request. Mixed error/proof,
   unexpected errors for the operation or malformed extras ⇒ `503 receipt_unavailable` with no payload echo and no
   further coordinator call. Valid pure errors and the existing authority binding are kept; no accepted authority is
   built from foreign evidence.
7. **Placement.** 7B-2 lives in `workflowRoutes.ts`; shared bounded helpers (body check with explicit admission time,
   payload/record digest, step/output table) may move to or be exported from `workflowProtocol.ts`. Response schemas
   are not widened to make probes pass. The coordinator's answer shapes do not change.
8. **Provenance.** Before editing, the writer copies the seven frozen workflow files to new scratch
   `%TEMP%/claude-dt7br1-writer/base/` and verifies they equal the starting hashes; `7b-r1-overlay.patch` is the exact

   byte-identical; `worker-manifest.sha256` is refreshed (still 189 Worker files) and the integration note updated.
9. **Docs.** Worker README workflow section, `38-cloud-workflows.md`, design `contract.md`/`test-matrix.md`/
   `first-slice.md` get corrected statements (interval admission, complete response proof, feed non-claim) and test

## DT-6B-3A-R1 ruling, storage protocol and file scope (planner, 17 Oct 21:02 AST)

Authority: `dashboard-remaining-tools-review.md` → "DT-6B-3A frozen review — changes required" and "Return to Claude
— DT-6B-3A-R1 authorized now" adopting `%TEMP%/dashboard-remaining-tools-2026-10-16/dt6b3a-review/
repair-contract-authorized.md` (SHA256 `3c068be4…`). Fixed refs unchanged (cached base; live deployment unverified).

**Storage/version protocol (3A-1), existing `SOCIAL_KV` only — no new DO/namespace/binding/migration.**
- Connection reference `tiktokads:account` (sealed as today) is written ONLY by a successful OAuth callback. New
  format: sealed `{ v: 2, connection: <random 128-bit hex id minted per callback>, token }`. Legacy format (sealed bare
  token, no `v`) is read as `{ connection: "legacy", token }`; it is never rewritten by refresh.
- Refresh never writes `tiktokads:account`. It writes the renewed token, sealed, to
  `tiktokads:account-refresh:<connection>` as `{ connection, token }` with KV `expiration` bounded by the renewed
  `refresh_expires_at` (≤ 1 year), keyed by the connection id captured BEFORE the provider call.
- `readAccountToken` (shared by account status, music and the pinned music probe): read the reference → connection id
  → read `tiktokads:account-refresh:<connection>`; use the refreshed token only when its sealed `connection` equals the
  reference's and its `open_id` equals the reference token's `open_id`; otherwise the reference token. A stale refresh
  for connection A lands under A's own key and is never read once the reference names connection B (fresh id per
  callback, also for a same-account reconnect), so it cannot replace B. Legacy: refresh lands under `…:legacy`, read
  only while the reference is still legacy; the first callback moves the reference to a fresh v2 id (no conversion step,
  no race introduced).
- After a refresh, before the chart fetch, the music path re-reads the reference; if the connection id changed it
  returns an explicit `409 { error: "account_changed" }` (no chart fetch with obsolete credentials, no cache write).
- Honest limits (README + tool 37): KV is eventually consistent, so account switching is not linearizable — a reader in
  another location may briefly see the previous reference; two concurrent refreshes of the SAME connection may still
  race on the provider refresh token (inherited upstream note). Old refresh keys expire by TTL; a callback may
  best-effort delete the previous connection's refresh key (not required for correctness). Missing/malformed/sealing
  or persistence failures fail honestly (`refresh_failed` / `not_connected`), credentials never in responses/logs.

**Malformed chart (3A-2).** Require `Array.isArray(data.list)` before normalization; missing/null/object list →
retrieval failure (`502 { error: "upstream", detail: "malformed_list" }` or the module's existing failure shape) with
ZERO successful chart-cache writes; a valid empty array stays a legitimate empty result (cacheable); ordering, valid rows,
query/cache separation and the public result shape unchanged.

**Files.** `workers/scout/src/tiktokAccount.ts` + `tiktokAccount.test.ts` (the two repairs, minimal helpers; the
upstream line-300 `if` reflow allowed, labelled nonsemantic); `workers/scout/src/tiktokMusicProbe.test.ts` only for
shared-reader compatibility (production `tiktokMusicProbe.ts` pinned); `workers/scout/README.md` account-storage text;
`planning/collaboration/dt6b3a-candidate/*` refreshed (patch, full manifest, classification relabelling the account

## DT-6B-2C-5B-R1 ruling and file scope (planner, 17 Oct 19:35 AST)

Authority: `dashboard-remaining-tools-review.md` → "DT-6B-2C-5B frozen review — changes required" (5B-1…5B-5) and
"Return to Claude — DT-6B-2C-5B-R1 authorized now" adopting `%TEMP%/dashboard-remaining-tools-2026-10-16/
dt6b2c5b-review/repair-contract-authorized.md` (SHA256 `f09d8bef…`). First repair round of C5B; app only.

Rulings:
- **5B-1 (Status vs pending).** Every Status and mutation response carries the `actionId` + `pending` snapshot it
  started with. Durable settlement goes through a store CAS that removes `pending` ONLY when (a) the stored pending
  equals the one this response belongs to (same action id) AND (b) the response is definitive for it: the mutation's
  own success/conflict answer, or a Status whose revision is greater than the pending `expectedRevision` (the Worker
  revision moved, so the pending request can no longer apply), or a Status at `expectedRevision` whose mode already
  equals the requested mode (no-op/applied). A Status at `expectedRevision` with the opposite mode, or any Status
  that started before the pending action was written, updates mode/counts only (when newer) and leaves `pending`
  untouched → uncertainty retained, further mutation blocked, Check-status-only. Lost POST answer then still marks the
  pending action uncertain. No automatic retry; no attribution.
- **5B-2 (conflict durability).** `recordConflict` returns the store disposition `{ ok, current }`; the hook paints the
  conflict only when the committed record equals the conflict it wrote; otherwise it reconciles to `current` with
  superseded or save-failure copy + Check status, retaining pending when unresolved. A conflict older than stored proof
  never paints its old mode/revision. Narrow conflicts never manufacture counts.
- **5B-3 (restore invariants).** Control import validation: same `origin|account|conversation` key with the same
  `handleId` must keep the stored immutable `recipientId` (contradiction → that entry rejected and the import reports
  it; local entry kept); a pending block must be internally consistent (`expectedRevision` ≤ the entry's own revision
  and `requestedMode` ∈ {auto, human}; for `register` no expected revision) else reject the entry; merge keeps the newer
  mode/revision (by revision) and keeps any local unresolved pending/uncertain separately; an imported pending is kept
  only if consistent with the merged (newer) revision. Valid higher-revision restore, legacy backups without the slice
  and explicit registration refresh stay compatible.
- **5B-4 (restore race).** Control slice import runs inside the same locked `commitFresh` coordination used by control
  mutations: fresh durable read of controls → merge → write → read-back verify before success; failure reports
  honestly and preserves recovery. If this makes import async, `SettingsScreen.tsx` confirmation (narrow exception)
  awaits it, disables double confirmation while busy, and reports rejection; necessary type/caller adjustments only.
- **5B-5 (review counts).** The cached full view is bound to the exact durable snapshot (`observedAt` + revision +
  counts) it committed; a review opens with cached rows only when the stored entry still equals that snapshot;
  otherwise it drops cached rows and shows the latest stored totals labelled "as last checked" with rows "not loaded".
  No silent extra request, no fabricated zeros.

needed (parity); appended `e2e/inbox.spec.ts`; tool 37; this handoff. Narrow exception (only if import becomes async;
record before editing): `components/settings/SettingsScreen.tsx` confirmation await/busy/error handling + focused tests

  Check status; pending stays when it was not durably let go. No counts.

  same revision with another mode; state comes from the higher revision; local pending/uncertain always kept (combined
  with newer imported state under a new commit id); an imported pending kept only when still open against the merged
  revision (register: no handle).

  rejected: string[] } | { ok: false; reason: "not-persisted" }>`. Under the same `3z-prod-articles` lock commitFresh
  holds: fresh durable read of the control slice → merge → one write → read-back (epoch + every control commit) →
  rollback and `not-persisted` if not kept. Without Web Locks no control action can persist (each refuses as
  unsupported), so the same steps run at once (keeps jsdom/legacy callers synchronous). **Narrow exception (recorded

  review's render) shows its rows only while the stored entry still has that commit, else stored totals "as last
  checked" with rows "not loaded".

## DT-6B-2C-4-R1 ruling and file scope (planner, 17 Oct 15:58 AST)

Authority: `dashboard-remaining-tools-review.md` → "DT-6B-2C-4 frozen review — changes required" (2C4-1…5) and
"Return to Claude — DT-6B-2C-4-R1 authorized now". First repair round of C4; app only; C5 not started.

Rulings:
- **2C4-1 (conditional cleanup).** Every preparing-cleanup site (failed Prepare, stale `not_found` captured while
  preparing, any analogous path) deletes the handle only through a new store action
  `clearInboxInstagramSendOpIf(scopeKey, expected: { operationId, state: "preparing", receiptVersion, commitId? })`
  that, inside the same locked `commitFresh`, compares the current disk handle and deletes only if it is still that
  exact unchanged preparing record; otherwise it keeps the newer same-operation proof and returns `{ ok: false,
  current }`; the hook then reconciles the view to `current` (superseded copy + Check status). A stale completion
  never erases recovery after a request may have sent.
- **2C4-2 (prepared status vs pending Confirm).** Store state order distinguishes `confirming` (local pending-confirm
  mark) from `prepared`: a write of `prepared` over `confirming|dispatching|unknown|sent|rejected|already_claimed`
  is refused regardless of version (generic status cannot undo a pending/uncertain Confirm). Only two explicit,
  named transitions may move `confirming → prepared`: (a) `rollbackBeforeRequest` — the hook's own pre-fetch fence
  failed and no Confirm request was issued; (b) `rollbackOnPreClaimRefusal` — that specific Confirm request returned
  a conclusively pre-claim refusal (allowlisted codes: `no_permission`, `stale`, `account_mismatch`,
  `target_unverified`, `target_invalid`, `token_expired`, `expired` with the intent still `prepared` in the answer,
  `text_invalid`, `conflict`, `capacity`). Both take the captured confirming record as the CAS expectation. A
  prepared Status while `confirming` keeps `confirming`, shows status-only recovery (no Send). Terminal/dispatching/
  unknown/cancel races unchanged; no automatic resend.
- **2C4-3 (rollback read-back).** Both rollback paths apply the view only when `back.ok` AND `back.current` equals the
  written prepared record (operation id + version + state); otherwise reconcile to `back.current` with superseded
  copy + Check status.
- **2C4-4 (comment/editor visit fence).** The action context gains `commentVisit` — a token minted whenever the
  selected comment (same media) changes, the editor/draft box for that comment unmounts or remounts, or the
  Inbox tab/page changes; captured at click, rechecked after each await and immediately before fetch; A→B→A mints a
  new token so a held action never revives. Wiring: `CommentsView.tsx` provides the token (and a focused test with
  real selection changes); `DraftBox.tsx`/`InboxScreen.tsx` touched only if the editor/tab visit cannot be conveyed
  from `CommentsView` — record the reason before editing. Plain Close still makes zero Cancel requests and keeps
  unresolved work recoverable.
- **2C4-5 (state-proof table).** `lib/inboxInstagramSend.ts` gets a strict required/forbidden field table per public
  state derived from real `scout.handle` fixtures of `inboxSendInstagram.ts`: `prepared` — no `claimedAt`/`settledAt`/
  `providerReplyId`/failure/unknown fields; `dispatching` — `claimedAt` required, no settlement fields; `sent` —
  `claimedAt`, `settledAt`, `providerReplyId` required, no failure/unknown; `rejected` — `failureCode` required, no
  `providerReplyId`; `unknown` — `unknownReason` required, `settledAt` optional (lost-receipt form), no
  `providerReplyId`; `already_claimed` — winning actor required, no own claim/settle proof; `cancelled`/`expired` — no
  `claimedAt`/`settledAt`/`providerReplyId`; integer `receiptVersion ≥ 1`. Contradictions → malformed (no handle
  removal, no terminal paint; retained handle + Check status). All eight genuine states and both unknown forms stay
  accepted.

Authority: `dashboard-remaining-tools-review.md` → "Return to Claude — DT-6B-2C-4 authorized now" adopting the
read-only contract `%TEMP%/dashboard-remaining-tools-2026-10-16/dt6b2c3-r1-review/next-packet.md` (SHA256
`78f6d2e4…`), points 1–7. App only; every Worker file, route, coordinator, poll/reply behavior, reader/provider/OAuth

**Gates (stated before implementation).** `lib/inboxInstagramSend.ts` exports `instagramSendReadiness()` returning
the literal `permission_unverified`, independent of reader capabilities, saved scopes, `canReply`, settings and
receipts; the hook takes `{ readiness }` as an injectable dependency defaulting to that function; tests inject

**Binding contract details (from the accepted backend).**
- Two generations: the reader generation (HMAC-derived, from the Instagram read) fences UI visits/account; the
  send generation (`ig-send-gen|account|stamp`) is learned from the prepared intent and bound thereafter. Never
  compare them; never treat reader generation as send authority.
- Text: trim only, ≤ 1000 code points; digest = SHA-256 of the exact trimmed text (via `lib/digest.ts`); NOT the DM
  NFC/body rules. Review shows the Worker-returned canonical text (internal whitespace/CRLF/Unicode preserved).
- Wire states: `prepared`, `dispatching`, `sent`, `rejected`, `unknown`, `already_claimed`, `expired`, `cancelled`;
  `unknown` may derive from a `dispatching` intent without a settled timestamp (do not require it); `sent` requires
  a non-empty `providerReplyId`; `already_claimed` names the owning actor (automatic/manual/retired); mixed

## DT-6B-2C-3-R1 ruling and file scope (Fable 5.1, 17 Oct 14:33 AST)

Authority: `dashboard-remaining-tools-review.md` → "DT-6B-2C-3 frozen review — changes required" (2C3-1…6) and
"Return to Claude — DT-6B-2C-3-R1 authorized now". First repair round of C3; repair complete validator/state
contracts, not individual fixtures.

Rulings:
- **2C3-1 (ownership pages).** In the new ownership chain only: every page is accepted only when it is a plain
  object with no `error` key at all (an `error` key of any value, incl. `null`/`false`, refuses); a response that
  carries an identity (`id`) different from the requested conversation/message refuses (`target_invalid`); duplicate
  message ids on one page with conflicting timestamps/senders refuse as ambiguous; absent/outside-first-page stays
  `target_unverified`. Applies to Prepare, Confirm re-proof and control registration before any mutation, claim or
  POST. The pinned generic helper is untouched.
- **2C3-2 (owner identity).** The owner is identified only by the fresh `/me user_id`; username equality never
  removes a sender from the customer set. A page where a non-owner id carries the owner's username, or any sender
  whose id/username pairing contradicts another row, fails closed (`target_invalid`, ambiguous identity). Exactly one
  distinct non-owner sender id is required.
- **2C3-3 (intent receipts).** One strict state-proof table for intents: required AND forbidden fields per state
  (`prepared`: no claim/settle fields; `dispatching`: `claimedAt`, no outcome fields; `sent`: `claimedAt`,
  `settledAt`, `providerMessageId`, no failure/unknown fields; `rejected`: `failureCode`, no `providerMessageId`;
  `unknown`: `unknownReason`; `already_claimed`/`cancelled`/`expired`: their own fields only). Version monotonicity
  bound to request-known proof: claim answer version must be exactly `knownVersion + 1`; settlement version must be
  greater than the claim version; any regression or contradiction → pre-dispatch invalid (zero POST,
  `receipt_unavailable`) or post-dispatch pending/uncertain (no replay). Complete terminal offline recovery and
  valid same-outcome `settled: false` preserved.
- **2C3-4 (control CAS answers).** Takeover answer must show `mode: "human"`; resume answer `mode: "auto"`;
  `changed: true` ⇒ `revision === expectedRevision + 1`; `changed: false` (genuine no-op) ⇒ `revision ===
  expectedRevision` and mode already the requested one; anything else → `receipt_unavailable`. A `conflict` answer
  is returned as a pure conflict `{ revision }` plus the verified handle's own target (account/conversation/
  recipient from the control row); any foreign conversation in the answer refuses. CAS never rerun; no provider
  calls; no credentials needed.
- **2C3-5 (control + in-flight proofs).** Control status requires the complete typed handle (`handleId`, `account`,
  `conversationId`, `recipientId`, `registeredGeneration`, `evidenceDigest`, timestamps, `revision`, `mode`); each
  in-flight row requires the complete claimed-effect shape with `state: "claimed"` only (settlement fields forbidden)
  and its account/conversation/recipient equal to the handle's; mismatch refuses the whole answer
  (`receipt_unavailable`); bounded rows/`inFlightTotal`/`inFlightTruncated` kept.
- **2C3-6 (handle activity).** `instagramDmCoordinator.ts`: `controlStatus` (successful read through a verified
  handle) updates the control row's `last_used_at` in its own small write (no mode/revision/effect change, no CAS
  rerun, no provider call); unused-handle purge keys on `last_used_at`; day-89 use survives day-91 purge; truly
  unused handles still purge at 90 days.

  recipient, generation, evidenceDigest)` → opaque `handle_id` (converges on the same verified target);

  existing conversation CAS keyed through the handle; in-flight output bounded: `inFlight` rows ≤ `CONTROL_ROWS_MAX`

Ruling:
- A pre-claim failure (`dm-claim-store` / `dm-account`) still retries up to `MAX_RETRIES` with the tick stop, as
  today. On the third (final) failure the item becomes **given up**: a timestamped terminal marker is recorded and
  the tick still stops (nothing after it is attempted this tick). On any later reread of the same conversation
  boundary a given-up item is **not attempted and does not restart its count**: it is treated as handled without a
  claim (`handledUpTo = item.ms`, no new log row — the three failure rows already exist, no `out.failed`), and the
  loop continues to the next item, so later valid same-time items progress. No cursor advance past an unattempted
  item; no manufactured claimed/sent effect; transient recovery before exhaustion unchanged; claimed/unknown effects
  never replayed; counts truthful; cap/budget/window/baseline/matching unchanged.
- Terminal marker (narrow exception, recorded here before editing): optional backward-compatible private field
  `PollState.givenUp?: Record<string, string>` (message id → ISO time of that message, `item.ms`). `replies.ts`
  changes ONLY: the type declaration, `{}` default in the initial state and load normalization (missing → `{}`),
  and expiry cleanup at poll start (drop entries whose time is older than `WINDOW_MS` relative to `now`). Bounded
  cleanup also in `answerInbox`: once a conversation's checkpoint `upTo` is ≥ a given-up item's time, delete its
  marker (the cursor has passed it). Existing `state.retries` keeps counts < `MAX_RETRIES` only (deleted on final
  as today). No other `replies.ts` line changes; comment loop, DM dispatch seam, poll scheduling, public wire,
  provider behavior untouched.

  typed `error.code` is `unknown` (classified before the definite-refusal branch); cooldown stays reserved; the
  original inbound effect never reopens; genuine typed refusal keeps releasing the cooldown.

  toward the subrequest pool; no limit change.

Rulings:

  every field typed (`operationId`, `account`, `generation`, `mediaId`, `commentId`, `digest`, `draftRevision`,

  timestamps for the same exact submission — still must match these fields); Confirm/settlement binds the

  trusted as proof, even with matching `claimed`/`settled`/`effect`: claim → invalid proof → zero POST (auto:

  `receipt_unavailable`); settlement → uncertainty retained, count zero. Keep genuine known errors (pure error
  envelope) mapped as before and keep the valid `settled: false` + matching durable effect as proof of the same
  already-durable outcome. Manual handler consumes the same helper validators.

Rulings:

  `prepare`/`claimConfirm` reads token and status together (one `Promise.all`), then re-reads the token once more
  after status; prepare/claim proceed only if token access string, token `userId`-independent account identity
  (the `/me user_id` already proved) and status `connectedAt` all equal the values captured at request start AND
  the two token reads are identical; otherwise `stale` with zero prepare/claim/provider write. No digest/generation
  `await` after that fence (compute digest before it).
- **2C1-2 (fresh clock).** `now()` is called anew at eligibility, review-expiry, token-expiry, claim and settlement
  boundaries (never the request-start `at`); expiry after the ownership GETs → `expired`, zero POST; token expiry
  crossing an await → `token_expired` before claim; receipts stamp the fresh time. `routes.ts`: pass a live clock
  (`() => new Date()` / `Date.now`) into the Instagram handler factory instead of a constant closure; narrow wiring.
- **2C1-3 (redirects).** Dispatch `fetch` uses `redirect: "manual"`; any 3xx → `unknown` with reason `redirect`,
  no second request, token never re-sent. Tests: 307 and 308 across two loopback origins → exactly one POST.
- **2C1-4 (typed refusal).** `rejected` only when the body is an object with `error` object whose `code` is a
  finite integer (and optional string `message`/`error_subcode` number); mapping to known codes unchanged; anything
  else (`{error:{}}`, `{error:[]}`, string code, missing code) → `unknown` with reason `malformed`, effect retained.
  Automatic stop policy for valid numeric refusals preserved.
- **2C1-5 (coordinator proof binding).** The shared client (`instagramPublicSend.ts`) parses every coordinator
  answer against the request: claim answer must carry `{ account, commentId, actor, state: "claimed", receiptVersion:
  int }` matching the request to count as won; `{ claimed: true }` alone or foreign identity → treated as invalid
  proof → zero POST, result `not_configured`/`detail: "public-claim-store"` for auto, `receipt_unavailable` for
  manual. Settlement answer must echo account, commentId, actor, requested outcome/state, provider reply id when
  `sent`, integer version; otherwise uncertainty retained, `publicReplies` not incremented; a repeated settlement
  accepted only if the durable row already shows the same outcome. Manual handler uses the same binding.
- **2C1-6 (scrub).** `replies.ts` passes the optional seal/secret to the helper; the public branch's `entry.detail`,
  `lastErrorDetail`, settlement detail and owner responses use the helper's sanitized detail only (token and seal
  scrubbed); error-code mapping preserved; legacy DM logging untouched.
- **2C1-7 (cleanup for auto-only).** The coordinator runs the bounded transactional purge (settled rows older than
  90 days → tombstones; claimed/unknown never purged) from `claimAuto` and `settleEffect` as well as `prepare`, at
  most once per N calls or when the last purge is older than one hour (cheap check), keeping tombstones permanent.

## DT-6B-2B-2-R1 ruling and file scope (Fable 5.1, 17 Oct 08:18 AST)

Authority: `dashboard-remaining-tools-review.md` → "DT-6B-2B-2 frozen review — changes required" (2B2-1…2B2-6)
and "Return to Claude — DT-6B-2B-2-R1 authorized now". First repair round of 2B-2. Readiness closed; capability
literal unchanged; Worker, `lib/inbox.ts`, wire test, `useProviderInbox.ts`, `useInbox.ts`, YouTube send
transport/hook/sheet, OAuth, package/lock pinned.

Rulings:
- **2B2-1 (immutable publishedId).** Three layers: `bindThreadsIntent` expectations include known `publishedId`
  (and known `containerId`) — any change at any version → mismatch, original proof retained, view "receipt mismatch"
  + Check status; the store action `setInboxThreadsSendOp` refuses a write that changes a stored non-empty
  `publishedId` or `containerId` for the same operation regardless of version/state; hook treats that refusal like
  a CAS refusal (reconcile to stored). Also harden the advisory direct-store probes: same-operation writes that
  change `account`, `draftRevision` or `digest` are refused.
- **2B2-2 (post-write same-op race).** `setInboxThreadsSendOp` returns `{ ok, current }` where `current` is the
  handle actually read back after the commit; the hook applies a view ONLY when `current.operationId`,
  `current.receiptVersion` and `current.state` equal the answer it just wrote (exact commit match); otherwise
  reconcile to `current` with superseded copy + Check status. Applies to settle, canonical Prepare and status.
- **2B2-3 (handle-only recovery).** Recovery (status GET, recovery list, Check status) keys on the handle's stored
  `account` + the configured Worker origin stored in the handle (`workerOrigin`), not on the currently loaded
  provider account; mount the recovery list in `ProviderView.tsx` even when the account read failed or another
  account is loaded, as long as `handle.workerOrigin === config().workerOrigin` (cross-origin handles are listed as
  "from another Worker, cannot check here" with no request). Status requests send the current bearer only to the
  matching configured origin; connection/visit/latest-action fences stay. Prepare/Confirm/Resume keep the loaded-
  account/generation/readiness checks. Recovery never grants write capability. Add `workerOrigin` to the handle
  schema (additive, default-less → handles without it are treated as the current origin on first read and
  rewritten once).
- **2B2-4 (Clear sync).** Successful Clear (from the recovery list or the row) publishes `{ scopeKey, revision }`
  through a tiny in-memory event in the Threads hook/store layer; every mounted `DraftBox` for that scope resets its
  base and text ONLY if its base revision equals the cleared revision and its text equals the submitted text;
  newer typing is kept and remains saveable (base becomes "none"); failed discard emits nothing. Reuse the existing
  `onCleared` path where it exists; shared `DraftBox` change must keep Instagram/YouTube behavior (tests).
- **2B2-5 (expiry loop).** `ThreadsSendReview` fires the automatic expiry `onEnd` at most once per
  `(operationId, reviewExpiresAt)` (ref-guarded), only when the server deadline is past by the client clock; a
  `prepared` answer after that never re-triggers; `check` callback memoised. Manual Check status always available.
- **2B2-6 (manual Check status everywhere).** Every retained-operation view (review/prepared, confirming,
  creating, created, publishing, unknown_*, superseded, save-failed) renders Check status via the shared
  `actions()` helper; it only runs `check` (latest-action fenced), never prepare/confirm/cancel. Closing the sheet
  never cancels; Cancel is an explicit button on `prepared` only.

## DT-6B-2B-1 plan — Threads reviewed reply, Worker only (Fable 5.1, 17 Oct 06:42 AST)

Authority: `dashboard-remaining-tools-review.md` → "Return to Claude — DT-6B-2B-1 authorized now" (bounded
contract, primary-source notes [1]–[3], partition). Backend only; app source and exports pinned; UI is 2B-2.

**Outcome.** Worker routes that let a later client prepare an immutable reviewed plain-text reply to one exact
direct reply under an owned Threads post, confirm it through two atomically claimed stages (create TEXT container
with `reply_to_id`, then publish `creation_id`), and recover status after any uncertainty without ever repeating a
stage. Production preparation fails closed (`permission_unverified`) until endpoint-specific grant evidence exists.

**Design.**
- `workers/scout/src/social/threadsSendCoordinator.ts`: SQLite Durable Object `ThreadsSendCoordinator`, one per
  `threads|<userId>`. Tables `intents(operation_id PK, submission_key UNIQUE-partial, account, generation, root_post_id,
  reply_to_id, text, digest, draft_revision, state, review_expires_at, created_at, updated_at, create_claimed_at,
  container_id, created_at_provider, publish_claimed_at, published_id, failure_code, failure_detail,
  unknown_reason, receipt_version)`, `tombstones`. States: `prepared → creating → created → publishing → published`
  plus `rejected`, `cancelled`, `expired`, `unknown_creation`, `unknown_publication`. Methods: `prepare` (idempotent
  by operation id + payload; converge on `account|draft_revision|reply_to_id|digest`; conflict on changed payload),
  `claimCreate` (`UPDATE … WHERE state='prepared' RETURNING`), `recordContainer(operationId, containerId)`
  (`creating → created`, persisted before any publish claim), `claimPublish` (`created → publishing RETURNING`),
  `settle` (`publishing → published` only with non-empty string `published_id`; `creating|publishing → rejected`
  with code; `creating → unknown_creation`; `publishing → unknown_publication`), `cancel` (`prepared` only),
  `get`. `receipt_version` increments on every write. Unknown states never purged, never re-claimable, never
  reused by convergence. 90-day purge of `published|rejected|cancelled|expired` with tombstones. No network inside.
- `workers/scout/src/social/inboxSendThreads.ts`: routes `POST /social/inbox/threads/send/prepare`
  `{ operationId, sendRef, text, draftRevision }`, `POST …/send/confirm` `{ operationId, digest, account }`,
  `GET …/send/:operationId?account=`, `POST …/send/:operationId/cancel`. Prepare: bearer/origin → token present and
  not expired → eligibility gate → `sendRef` seal (domain `send-target-v1|threads`, `INBOX_SEAL_SECRET`) binds
  `{ account, generation, rootPostId, replyToId }` and must match current account/generation → text trimmed,
  1–`THREADS_SEND_TEXT_MAX = 500` chars (local product policy; documented as not a verified provider limit) → ONE
  bounded preflight GET of `/{replyToId}?fields=id,root_post,replied_to` verifying `root_post.id === rootPostId`
  (missing/mismatched ancestry → `target_invalid`; 404 → `not_found`) → DO `prepare` (10 min expiry). Zero POSTs.
  Confirm: revalidate bearer, token, generation, digest, expiry → `claimCreate` → one `POST /me/threads` with
  `media_type=TEXT`, `text`, `reply_to_id` (no `auto_publish_text`; 15 s abort; `PAGE_BYTES_MAX` answer) → 2xx with
  non-empty string `id` and no `error` → `recordContainer`; refusal with Meta error body → `rejected`; timeout /
  network / 5xx / malformed / `error`+`id` → `unknown_creation`. Then `claimPublish` → one `POST /me/threads_publish`
  with `creation_id=<stored container>` → 2xx string `id` → `published`; refusal → `rejected`; else
  `unknown_publication`. Receipt write failure after a provider success → the matching unknown state. A confirm on
  `created` (container durable, publish never claimed) re-validates eligibility/review and continues from
  `claimPublish` only — never recreates. Concurrent confirms return the current state. Status/cancel: zero external
  writes; cancel cannot claim an in-flight stage. Optional bounded `GET …/send/:op/container` reconciliation is
  OUT of 2B-1 (record as follow-up). Body read through the 2A streaming byte budget (`16_384`); scrub token and
  seal from every error path like the YouTube module.
- Eligibility gate: `inboxSendThreads.ts` exports a handler factory taking `{ fetch, now, eligibility }`.
  Default `eligibility` returns `{ ok: false, reason: "permission_unverified" }` with a readiness note; tests inject
  `{ ok: true }` to exercise the protocol. No env flag, no browser bypass, no inference from `TH_SCOPES`,
  stored scope strings or `canPublish`. Route maps the default to `no_permission` with `detail:
  "permission_unverified"`. Missing binding → `not_configured` `detail: "receipt-store"`; seal → `"seal"`; KV → `"kv"`.
- `inboxReadThreads.ts` (additive): direct replies under an owned root post gain `sendRef` only when
  `root_post.id` is the owned post and `replied_to.id` is known (otherwise no ref); account route adds
  `capabilities.sendReplies` = `permission_unverified` (never `ok` in this packet). Read GETs stay pure.
- Wiring: `wrangler.jsonc` binding `THREADS_SEND_COORDINATOR` → class `ThreadsSendCoordinator`, migration
  `v2-threads-send` with `new_sqlite_classes`; `index.ts` adds exactly one more named export and amends the comment;
  `store.ts` `SocialEnv.THREADS_SEND_COORDINATOR?: DurableObjectNamespace`; `routes.ts` narrow dispatch.
  `sendCoordinator.runtime.test.ts` may update only its exact binding/class-list expectation.
- Tests: `threadsSendCoordinator.test.ts` (node:sqlite-style unit as YouTube's), `inboxSendThreads.test.ts` (fake

## DT-6B-2A-R2 ruling and file scope (Fable 5.1, 17 Oct 06:10 AST)

Authority: `dashboard-remaining-tools-review.md` → "DT-6B-2A-R1 frozen review — changes required", residuals
2A-R1-A…D and "Return to Claude — DT-6B-2A-R2". Second repair round, client/UI only. Worker, coordinator,
binding, readers, `useInbox.ts` pinned; Worker evidence reused after pin check.

Rulings:
- **A (provider switch).** The captured action context in `useSend.ts` gains the active provider and a per-visit
  token (a value that changes on every `setInboxProvider`/account/scope-session change). Re-check after every
  `await` and immediately before `fetch`; mismatch → zero requests, action `closed`, local `dispatching` mark rolled
  back to `prepared` only when nothing was sent. Switching away and back mints a new visit token, so an abandoned
  action can never resume; a durable handle for an already-dispatched operation is kept for status recovery.
  Observe provider from the send layer (the store's `inboxProvider` / existing scope inputs); touch
  `useProviderInbox.ts` only for a read-only visit accessor if strictly needed — record the necessity first.
- **B (refused receipt shown).** `record()` returns `{ ok, current }` (current durable handle after the attempt).
  Prepare/Confirm/Status/Cancel apply the view ONLY when `ok` is true and the response's `operationId` equals the
  current handle's; otherwise the view reconciles to `current` (same scope): a replaced/settled operation shows
  that durable state with Check status for the current operation, never success for a replaced one, never a review
  with Send over newer uncertainty. Store action keeps its existing CAS (operationId + receiptVersion + state order);
  extend `store/index.ts` only to return the current handle from the action if it does not already.
- **C (immutable target binding).** `SendExpect`/`bindIntent` in `lib/inbox.ts` also compare `parentCommentId`,
  `videoId`, `threadId` when the caller knows them (from the reviewed intent or the row's `sendRef` payload returned
  by prepare); a known mismatch → original handle retained, `unknown`-style recoverable view with Check status. Status
  from a known review passes the known target too. Handle-only recovery (reload, no intent) compares only what it has
  (scope + operationId) and does not invent fields. Canonical convergence for the same submission key still passes.
- **D (recovery without write permission).** `SendReview.tsx` renders operation controls (state line + Check status)
  from the retained handle regardless of `capabilities.sendComments` or a missing `sendRef`; only the new-send path
  (Prepare/Send) is gated. `ProviderView.tsx`/`DraftBox.tsx` keep the opener enabled when a handle exists for the
  row even if sending is unavailable; copy explains "sending unavailable; checking an earlier send". No prepare or
  confirm from recovery.

Files: `components/social/inbox/{useSend.ts,SendReview.tsx}` + tests; `lib/inbox.ts` + test; `DraftBox.tsx`,

## DT-6B-2A-R1 ruling and file scope (Fable 5.1, 17 Oct 05:28 AST)

Authority: `dashboard-remaining-tools-review.md` → "DT-6B-2A frozen review — changes required", findings
2A-1…2A-11 and "Return to Claude — DT-6B-2A-R1". Repair all eleven; no provider feature, no change to the
one-attempt coordinator model. Reproduce each finding RED first (own probe or copy of Codex's into writer scratch;
Codex originals under `%TEMP%/dashboard-remaining-tools-2026-10-16/dt6b2a-review/` read-only).

Rulings:
- **2A-1 (P1).** Every action in `useSend.ts` captures `{ workerOrigin, token identity, provider, account, generation,
  configEpoch, scope session }` ONCE at the click, re-checks that capture against live `config()`/scope after every
  `await` (handle write, lock) and immediately before `fetch`; any mismatch → zero requests, action ends `closed`.
  Requests are built from the captured connection only, never from a re-read config.
- **2A-2.** Status/confirm completions apply only if `actionId` is the latest for that scope AND the response's
  `operationId` equals the handle's; a stale completion is dropped, never writes `closed` over a newer view. Durable
  handle updates carry a monotonic `receiptVersion` (store action compares `operationId` + `receiptVersion >= current`
  and forbids `sent|rejected → dispatching|prepared` regressions). Same-operation forward transitions still apply.
- **2A-3.** `setInboxSendOp` evicts only settled handles (`sent|rejected|cancelled|expired`), oldest first; if 50
  unresolved exist, the write is refused with `capacity` and the UI shows actionable copy (check or cancel pending
  sends). Updates to an existing handle always succeed.
- **2A-4.** `lib/inbox.ts` parsers take the expected identity: prepare response must match provider/account/
  generation/draftRevision/digest (and `text`) or be the canonical convergence for the same submission key; confirm/
  status/cancel responses must carry the same `operationId`; `sent` requires a non-empty string `providerCommentId`.
  Mismatch → keep the original handle, show `unknown`-style recoverable uncertainty (Check status), never success.
- **2A-5.** Cancel removes the handle only on a parsed `cancelled|expired` for the same operation, or after a status
  that proves a settled outcome; network/5xx cancel → handle kept, state shows failure + Check status.
- **2A-6.** On convergence, write the canonical handle through `commitFresh` and open review only after read-back
  succeeds; failure → actionable persistence error, handle keeps the original id, no confirm enabled.
- **2A-7.** Recovery runs from the persisted handle alone (no saved draft, no intent needed): on open, `GET
  …/send/:op`; failed GET → `unknown` view with the uncertainty line and an enabled Check status for that operation;
  never prepare/resend.
- **2A-8.** Review shows the exact destination without new storage or coordinator change: parent comment id,
  `youtubeCommentLink(videoId, parentCommentId)`, parent author and a bounded excerpt taken from the loaded read row
  whose id equals the intent's `parentCommentId` (nested shortcut → mapped top-level parent, labelled); when no row is
  loaded, id + link + account still show. No fetched body enters the persisted handle.
- **2A-9.** After a successful Clear draft, the editor base and text reset to empty (newer unsaved input preserved
  if present); a failed discard reports failure and is not treated as cleared. Existing newer-revision control stays.
- **2A-10.** In `inboxSendYouTube.ts`, a 2xx body containing an `error` object (or any non-comment `kind` when
  present) is `unknown` even with an `id`; ordinary `{ id, snippet }` stays `sent`.
- **2A-11.** Read request bodies through a streaming byte budget (`BODY_BYTES_MAX = 16_384` bytes) that cancels
  the reader on overflow before parse, for prepare/confirm/cancel; valid Unicode JSON and `SEND_TEXT_MAX` unchanged.
- Nonblocking: scrub the seal secret like the read handler in the send module's error path (allowed, small).

## DT-6B-2A plan — reviewed YouTube public text reply path (Fable 5.1, 17 Oct 04:35 AST)

Acceptance: `dashboard-remaining-tools-review.md` → "Return to Claude — DT-6B-2A authorized now"

and DT-7–DT-10 remain required. No live send, grant, secret, remote provisioning or deployment.

**Outcome.** From a saved private draft on a YouTube top-level comment: Prepare (validates
account, grant, target, exact text; persists an immutable intent) → Review (EN/AR: account,
public destination, exact text) → explicit Send (one atomic `dispatching` claim, then one
provider POST) → durable receipt (`sent` with provider comment id / `rejected` / `unknown`) with
recovery after reload and no automatic resend.

**Worker.**
- Durable Object `SendCoordinator` (`workers/scout/src/social/sendCoordinator.ts`, SQLite-backed;
  `wrangler.jsonc` adds `durable_objects.bindings [{ name: "SEND_COORDINATOR", class_name:
  "SendCoordinator" }]` and `migrations [{ tag: "v1-send", new_sqlite_classes: ["SendCoordinator"] }]`;
  `index.ts` adds exactly one named export `export { SendCoordinator } …` — a Durable Object class
  is a legitimate workerd entrypoint; the module's warning is kept and amended; local runtime
  validation required). One object per `provider|accountId`. Tables `intents(operation_id PK,
  submission_key UNIQUE, provider, account, generation, thread_id, video_id, parent_comment_id,
  text, digest, draft_revision, state, review_expires_at, created_at, updated_at, claimed_at,
  dispatched_at, provider_comment_id, failure_code, failure_detail, unknown_reason)`. Methods
  (RPC via `fetch` or DO RPC): `prepare(op)` — same `operation_id` + same digest → same intent;
  same `operation_id` + different payload → `conflict`; different `operation_id` but same
  `submission_key` (`account|draft_revision|parent_comment_id|digest`) → returns the existing
  intent (converge); `claim(operation_id, digest)` — single transaction `prepared → dispatching`
  (also fails `expired`/`cancelled`/already `dispatching|sent|rejected|unknown` → returns current
  state, never a second claim); `settle(operation_id, outcome)` — writes `sent`/`rejected`/`unknown`
  once; `cancel` (`prepared` only); `get`. No network inside the DO. Retention: terminal rows
  kept 90 days then purged except `unknown`, which is never purged; purged `operation_id`s stay
  blocked through a `tombstones(operation_id, submission_key)` table so nothing becomes
  dispatchable again.
- Routes (`inboxSendYouTube.ts`, bearer + origin as `/social/*`): `POST /social/inbox/youtube/send/prepare`
  `{ operationId, sendRef, text, draftRevision }`; `POST …/send/confirm` `{ operationId, digest }`;
  `GET …/send/:operationId`; `POST …/send/:operationId/cancel`. Prepare: bearer/origin → stored
  token scope must contain `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.force-ssl` (else
  `no_permission`), token not expired (else `token_expired`; no refresh here), `sendRef` seal
  (domain `send-target-v1|youtube`, server-only `INBOX_SEAL_SECRET`) must match current
  account/generation, text bounded (`SEND_TEXT_MAX = 2000`, non-empty after trim, no normalization
  beyond trim and shown as-is), then ONE bounded preflight GET `commentThreads?part=snippet&id=
  <threadId>` verifying `snippet.videoId`, `snippet.channelId` (owned channel), `snippet.isPublic`,
  `snippet.canReply`, `snippet.topLevelComment.id === parentCommentId` → `target_invalid` /
  `not_public` / `not_replyable` / `not_found`; then DO `prepare` (review expiry 10 min). Zero

  classify: 2xx with string `id` → `sent`; documented 4xx (`insufficientPermissions`, `forbidden`,
  `commentsDisabled`, `processingFailure`, `badRequest`, quota) → `rejected` with code; timeout,
  network, 5xx, malformed 2xx (no id) → `unknown` (`unknown_reason`), intent stays
