  confirms return the existing state. Missing `SEND_COORDINATOR` binding → `not_configured` with
  `detail: "receipt-store"`; missing seal → `detail: "seal"`; missing KV → `detail: "kv"` (the
  readiness-copy caveat closes here for the send path).
- `inboxReadYouTube.ts` (additive): each thread row carries `sendRef` (sealed

**DT-6B-1-R2 (Fable ruling on residual B1-R1-A, 04:12 AST; same writer; product scope exactly
`components/social/inbox/useProviderInbox.ts` + test, `InboxScreen.tsx` + test only if the pending
state needs it, `e2e/inbox.spec.ts`, `planning/tools/36-inbox.md`, this handoff; `messages/inbox.*.json`
only if new pending copy is unavoidable. Worker, auth, transport, OAuth, storage, sync,
automation, publishing, Instagram reader and `useInbox.ts` pinned.)**
Chosen contract: **supersede.** An accepted Refresh (or any new read of the same parent list:
initial, paginated or refreshed) while that list has a pending request starts a NEW session
token for the list immediately and issues the fresh request; the older in-flight request is
orphaned — its settlement (success or error) can neither replace rows, release busy, nor
re-enable anything, because the existing session gate no longer matches. The busy state follows
the newest session; Refresh stays enabled (no silent discard, no disabled button). Nested reply
caches and in-flight reply sessions for the refreshed video are invalidated as in R1; private
drafts, useful rows on failure, independent per-comment coverage and on-demand reply loading
are preserved; navigation or a provider change during the wait applies the existing invalidation
(the superseding request is itself abandoned, never revived). Regressions (RED first, mirroring
Codex's accepted-button repro `dt6b1-r1-review/client/client.adversarial.test.ts` and
`browser/REFRESH-REPORT.md`, copied to writer scratch): Refresh #1 held → Refresh #2 accepted →
threads request count rises → release #1 (`obsolete`) → view shows `fresh` from #2; same with #1
settling as an error; initial-load pending then Refresh; paginated pending then Refresh (newer
page supersedes, no duplicate rows); navigation away / provider switch during the wait → neither
response lands; old settlement never releases busy of the newer session; e2e actual-button case
with a held threads response counting requests and asserting the fresh embedded reply. Checks:
app set (`pnpm vitest run lib/inbox.test.ts components/social/inbox store components/shell
components/tools messages lib/tools.test.ts`), `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, prettier,
`pnpm build`, `pnpm e2e e2e/inbox.spec.ts e2e/autoreplies.spec.ts e2e/settings.spec.ts` on
existing :3000; Worker evidence reused after pin check; then freeze, owner none, one queue message.
Readiness caveat recorded (not R2 scope): missing KV and missing seal both answer
`not_configured` while the copy names only the seal.

**DT-6B-1-R1 (Fable ruling on findings B1-1 … B1-8, 03:40 AST; same writer; production scope
exactly Codex's list: `inboxReadCommon.ts`, `inboxReadThreads.ts`, `inboxReadYouTube.ts`, narrow
`routes.ts` wiring for B1-1, `useProviderInbox.ts`, `ProviderView.tsx`, `lib/inbox.ts` parsers/
types and `parts.tsx`/`InboxScreen.tsx` only as needed; matching tests, `messages/inbox.*.json`,
README Inbox section, `36-inbox.md`, this handoff. Accepted Instagram reader/`useInbox`, auth,
OAuth, storage, sync, publishing, automation untouched.)**
1. B1-1 server-only sealing key for Threads/YouTube receipts and cursors: a new Worker secret
   `INBOX_SEAL_SECRET` (recorded configuration field; `wrangler secret`, never sent to the
   browser, never logged). `inboxReadCommon.ts` derives the HMAC key from it (domain-separated,
   `"inbox-seal-v1|" + provider`); `routes.ts` passes `env.INBOX_SEAL_SECRET` instead of the
   bearer. Fail safe: when the secret is missing, the own-content listings and every ref/cursor
   route of the two new providers return 503 `not_configured` with a README setup note (no ref
   is ever minted with the bearer). Instagram's DT-6A cursors (bound to the bearer holder's own
   account, no cross-resource authority) stay as accepted and are recorded as an inherited limit,
   not changed here. Tests: refs minted by an independent WebCrypto client holding the bearer and
   generation are rejected before any upstream call; genuine refs from a listing still work; the
   secret never appears in any response, scope, log or error.
2. B1-2 YouTube account envelope: success requires a JSON object with an explicit `items` array;
   `{}`, `{ items: null }`, `true` → `upstream` (unavailable), never "no channel"; genuine
   `{ items: [] }` → honest no-channel state; multiple channels still `needsSelection`.
3. B1-3 reply totals: `totalReplyCount` missing/null/non-numeric/negative → `totalReplies: null`
   (unknown, not zero). `ProviderView` shows "Load replies" whenever the total is unknown or
   greater than the embedded count; valid `0` hides it; partial embedded vs loaded stays distinct.
4. B1-4 id grammar: ids are accepted only as strings matching `ID_RE`, or as JSON numbers that
   are safe integers whose decimal string matches `ID_RE`; anything else makes the row invalid →
   malformed page (DT-6A-R2 rule); a successful page can never emit a ref the reader's own path
   check refuses (round-trip test).
5. B1-5 target sessions: every navigation (post → post, video → video, channel → channel, and
   leaving to `null`) invalidates the previous target's session and starts a fresh session token
   for the new visit; an abandoned response can neither block nor release the new request;
   completed cached rows for unchanged targets may stay.
6. B1-6 provider visits: account/open continuations carry a provider-visit token; switching
   providers invalidates them (no hidden posts read after a late account answer). On return to a
   provider, a selected view with no loaded rows is deliberately reset to the first list (posts/
   videos) rather than left empty; no old continuation is revived; no eager reply fan-out.
7. B1-7 refresh: refreshing a video's threads invalidates that video's expanded reply caches and
   their in-flight sessions; expanded lists reload on demand (Load replies), fresh embedded
   content is shown meanwhile; private drafts untouched. Regression covers late old replies,
   edits/deletions and count changes.
8. B1-8 per-comment coverage: after loading replies, each comment renders its own coverage
   footer (`more`/`cap`/`partial`/error/end with Load replies or Retry as applicable),
   independent of the parent list's footer; the parent "everything loaded" message never implies
   reply completion. Existing rows and retries preserved.
Tests: Codex's reproductions (11 Worker + 7 client + 1 browser) as regressions in the matching
suites (probes copied to writer scratch; originals untouched), plus controls (genuine refs,
true-empty channel list, valid zero totals, string ids, normal navigation, provider return with
loaded rows, refresh with unchanged replies). Checks: DT-6B-1 list + `pnpm worker:test`,
existing :3000 only; then freeze, owner none, one queue message.

## DT-5 plan (Fable 5.1, 16 Oct 22:48 AST) — two parts, one freeze

### Part A — Workflow → AutoPost bridge fix (Codex P1, app-side only)

Defect (Codex probe, provider calls 0): workflow outputs are posts with id `wf:<runId>:<actionId>`;
`lib/publish.ts` `buildJob` sends `id: post.id` unchanged, the deployed Worker validator
`/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}$/` (`workers/scout/src/social/publish.ts:86`, also on the run/cancel
path at `:481`) rejects it (schedule HTTP 400 `id`; run/cancel 404 because `%3A` stays encoded).
Fixing only one side is insufficient; the Worker on `origin/main` is deployed and must not be
required for this fix.

Ruling: a stable publish-id mapping on the app side, applied to EVERY lifecycle action.
- `lib/publish.ts`: `export function publishJobId(post: Pick<Post, "id" | "autoPost">): string` →
  `post.autoPost?.jobId` when present; else `post.id` when it already matches
  `PUBLISH_ID_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}$/` (copied from the Worker with a comment naming the
  source line); else `j-<sanitized>-<fnv1a32 hex of post.id>` where sanitized = post.id with every
  character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` replaced by `-`, truncated so the whole id is ≤ 100 chars
  (deterministic, collision-resistant through the hash suffix).
- `buildJob` uses `publishJobId(post)` as `id`. `scheduleAutoPost` (or wherever the job is
  remembered) stores `autoPost.jobId = publishJobId(post)` after a successful schedule.
  `usePublish.runNow`/`cancel`, `publishRun`/`publishCancel` callers and the auto-resync path all
  pass `publishJobId(post)`. The "jobs this browser does not follow" reconciliation (`lib/publish.ts`
  ~495–509) matches `job.id` against `publishJobId(post)` and remembered `autoPost.jobId`.
- Workflow outputs are unchanged (deterministic `wf:…` ids and receipts stay).
- Tests (RED first): `lib/publish.test.ts` — `publishJobId("wf:run:a1")` matches `PUBLISH_ID_RE`,
  is stable, differs for `wf:run:a2`, keeps safe ids unchanged, prefers remembered `jobId`;
  `buildJob` emits the mapped id; `encodeURIComponent(mappedId)` contains no `%`.
  `components/social/usePublish.test.ts` — schedule, run and cancel for a `wf:` post all hit the
  fake Worker with the same mapped id; remote job list reconciliation does not flag the post as
  unfollowed. `e2e/autopost.spec.ts` — one new case: a workflow-generated post scheduled through
  the Auto-post tab against the stubbed Worker (`page.route`), then Post now and Cancel resolve
  (no 400/404), zero provider calls. Keep Codex's probe files untouched.

### Part B — Business Kit at `/social/business`

**Outcome.** Replace the "soon" placeholder with a bilingual creator media kit (owner-editable,
real Growth numbers with provenance, preview + print/PDF + allowlisted JSON export) and a
brand-deal board. No fabricated metrics, logos, clients, prices or testimonials. Public
hosting is DT-8.

**Data model (`lib/domain.ts`, additive).**
```ts
const Bi = (max: number) => z.object({ ar: z.string().max(max), en: z.string().max(max) });
export const BusinessKitSchema = z.object({
  tagline: Bi(120).default({ ar: "", en: "" }),
  bio: Bi(600).default({ ar: "", en: "" }),
  contact: z.object({ email: z.string().max(120).default(""), website: z.string().max(200).default(""), location: Bi(80).default({ ar: "", en: "" }) }).default({}),
  services: z.array(z.object({ id, name: Bi(80), desc: Bi(240) })).max(8).default([]),
  rateCard: z.array(z.object({ id, deliverable: Bi(80), platform: PlatformSchema.optional(), priceSar: z.number().int().min(0).nullable().default(null), note: Bi(160).default({ ar: "", en: "" }) })).max(12).default([]),
  pastWork: z.array(z.object({ id, title: Bi(120), url: z.string().max(300).default(""), platform: PlatformSchema.optional(), day: z.string().regex(DAY_KEY_RE).optional() })).max(12).default([]),
  featuredPlatforms: z.array(PlatformSchema).default([]),       // which platforms the kit shows; empty = all with data
  estimator: z.object({ sarPerThousandFollowers: z.number().min(0).default(15), engagementMultiplier: z.number().min(0).default(1), deliverable: z.record(z.enum(["post","story","reel","video"]), z.number().min(0)).default({ post: 1, story: 0.5, reel: 1.5, video: 2 }) }).default({}),
  revision: int ≥1 default 1, commitId: z.string().min(1), updatedAt,
});
export const DEAL_STAGES = ["lead", "talking", "offer", "agreed", "delivered", "paid", "lost"] as const;
export const BrandDealSchema = z.object({ id, brand: z.string().min(1).max(120), contact: z.string().max(200).default(""), stage: z.enum(DEAL_STAGES).default("lead"), deliverable: z.string().max(200).default(""), valueSar: z.number().int().min(0).nullable().default(null), notes: z.string().max(1000).default(""), createdAt, updatedAt, commitId: z.string().min(1) });
```

**Amendment A (Codex "DT-5 resumed" review gates, received 23:02 AST; same writer, no new
scope).**
1. Remembered `autoPost.jobId` is reused only when it matches `PUBLISH_ID_RE`; an empty, colon or
   over-long remembered value (the import schema allows them) falls through to the mapping.
2. Digest: the FNV1a32 mapper collides (Codex's canonical pair in
   `%TEMP%/dashboard-publish-id-plan-probe-2026-10-16.cjs`/`.json`, both → `j-wf-run----------04591cb8`).
   Ruling: `j-<sanitized, ≤ 40 chars>-<first 24 hex of SHA-256 of the raw post id>` (≤ 100 chars).
   Reuse an existing synchronous digest helper in `lib/` if one exists; otherwise add a compact
   pure-JS SHA-256 in `lib/digest.ts` with the standard test vectors (`""`, `"abc"`). Plus
   collision ownership: `publishJobId(post, taken)` takes the set of job ids remembered by OTHER
   local posts (`autoPost.jobId`, and safe pass-through ids of other posts); when the candidate is
   in that set, append `-2`, `-3`, … deterministically until free (still ≤ 100). Remote/local
   reconciliation owns a remote job only when `post.autoPost.jobId === job.id` or the post's safe
   pass-through id equals it; a safe id equal to another post's generated id is covered by the
   same check. Applied to schedule, auto-resync, run, cancel and reconciliation. Tests: Codex's
   pair maps to different ids; remembered invalid id ignored; taken-set suffixing; safe id equal
   to a generated id does not steal the other post's job.
3. Future metrics: `kitMetrics` filters snapshots to `snapshot.day <= dayKey(now)` (and posts to
   `publishedAt <= now`) before calling `platformOverview`; test with an imported future snapshot.
4. First-save generation fence: the kit editor captures `base = { commitId: null, generation }`
   on mount even when no kit exists; `saveBusinessKit` rejects when the generation moved, and a
   `commitId: null` base is a conflict when a kit now exists in fresh state (a queued first save
   after reset/import never recreates discarded text).
5. Export/print freshness: Preview, Print and Export build the projection from the editor's
   CURRENT draft (plus live metrics); when the draft is unsaved the file name gets `-unsaved` and
   the UI says so; the previous persisted kit is never silently exported after a failed flush.
   Projection excludes deal contacts/notes, settings/keys, estimator internals and any other
   private data (deep allowlist test).

**Amendment B (Codex "DT-5 lifecycle / metric follow-up", received 23:04 AST; same writer,
source-only, no new scope).**
1. Cancel vs in-flight resync: a held auto-resync `POST /social/publish`, then a successful Cancel
   `DELETE`, then the released POST must leave the job cancelled. Clearing the debounce alone
   lets the late POST recreate it. Ruling: every resync carries a per-post resync token captured
   at send; `cancel` bumps the token (and remembers `autoPost.cancelledAt`/state) so a resync
   response or send that no longer matches the token is dropped; a resync never sends while the
   post is cancelled; if a stale resync did reach the Worker first, the cancel runs after it (the
   DELETE is sent after any in-flight resync settles, never concurrently). Test: held POST →
   DELETE ok → release → final state cancelled, exactly one DELETE, no re-schedule.
2. Engagement provenance: the kit's sample count and date range count only posts with
   `views > 0`, the same filter the existing Growth averages use (`lib/analytics.ts`); test that
   a zero-view post is excluded from both the number and the range.
3. Allocation durability for the suffixed ids: the chosen publish id (for example `C-2`) is
   captured into `autoPost.jobId` BEFORE the create request is sent (an allocation, not a
   success claim; a separate `autoPost.jobState`/pending flag records that the Worker has not
   confirmed). A lost response, taken-set change or reload therefore retries with `C-2`, never
   allocating `C`. Run and Cancel use only the remembered id and never allocate a new suffix for
   an existing remembered id; when a remembered id is missing on the Worker and ownership is
   ambiguous (the id is also a different post's remembered id, or a safe-id alias), the action
   blocks with an explicit error instead of deleting or running a different job. Reconciliation
   checks explicit remembered ownership FIRST and never lets a first-array safe-id alias steal
   another post's remembered job. Tests: schedule picks `C-2` → response lost → reload → retry
   sends `C-2`; run/cancel on a remembered id never suffixes; ambiguous ownership blocks; alias
   cannot steal explicit ownership.

**Rulings.** (1) Bridge fix is app-side mapping; the deployed Worker stays untouched and the
mapping also satisfies any future validator extension. (2) Metrics are per platform with their
own provenance; no pooled totals; snapshot views never shown. (3) Print-to-PDF through the
browser instead of a PDF library (no new dependency). (4) Estimator is explicitly the owner's
assumptions. (5) Deals keep history via stage `lost`; no delete. (6) Executor Opus 5.5.

## DT-6A plan — Instagram pure Inbox reads + private local drafts (Fable 5.1, 17 Oct 01:30 AST)

Acceptance: `dashboard-remaining-tools-review.md` → "Return to Claude — DT-6A authorized now"
(six boundaries) and the external contract `%TEMP%/dashboard-remaining-tools-2026-10-16/
dt6a-instagram-read-contract.md` (read-only). Threads/YouTube comments and any sending are DT-6B.

**Outcome.** `/social/inbox`: read-only Instagram conversations/messages and owned-media
comments through new pure Worker readers, with durable private drafts, Copy and validated
provider links. Opening, refreshing and paging never send, never mark seen, never touch the
reply automation's `replies:state`/`inboxSince`/cursors/logs. Studio's reminder Inbox stays
separate and unchanged.

**Worker (`workers/scout/src/social/inboxRead.ts`, new; routes GET only).** Bearer + CORS are
already enforced by `scout.ts` for `/social/*`; `routes.ts` dispatches `/social/inbox/...` to
`handleInboxRead(req, rest, store, now, reply, deps)` (non-GET → 405). Reuse `fetchJson`,
`metaBody`/`graph`, `clip`, `Store.getTokens("instagram")`, `toReplyCode` + `TICK_STOPPERS`
semantics from `replyCore` for error mapping — but never `readInbox`/`pollReplies` and never any
`Store.put*`.
- `GET /social/inbox/account` → `{ accountId, handle, generation, capabilities: { messages, comments } }`.
  `accountId` = `String(me.user_id)` from `/me?fields=user_id,username` (never username);
  `generation` = SHA-256 hex of `accountId + "|" + <non-secret connection stamp from the stored
  status/token metadata, e.g. connectedAt or tokenExpiresAt>` (never the token itself);
  `capabilities.*` ∈ `ok | no_permission | token_expired | rate_limited | not_eligible |
  not_connected | upstream`, derived from the granted scopes on the stored token set plus the
  last error of a cheap probe only when needed (no probe when scopes already say no).
- `GET /social/inbox/conversations?cursor=` → `{ accountId, generation, fetchedAt, items:
  [{ id, updatedAt | null, participants: [{ id, username? }] }], next: cursor | null, coverage }`.
  Upstream: `/{accountId}/conversations?platform=instagram&limit=20&fields=id,updated_time,participants{id,username}`
  (the automation's 20 is a page size here, not a history claim).
- `GET /social/inbox/conversations/:id/messages?cursor=` → `{ …, items: [{ id, createdAt | null,
  direction: "in" | "out" | "unknown", from: { id?, username? } | null, text, kind: "text" |
  "story_reply" | "story_mention" | "share" | "unsupported" | "empty" }], next, coverage }`.
  Upstream: the existing `messages{…}` expansion on `/{conversationId}?fields=messages.limit(20)
  {id,created_time,from,message,story,is_unsupported}`, with the nested edge's `after` cursor
  re-applied as `messages.after(<after>).limit(20)`; the bare-id expansion failure is reported as
  `coverage: "history_unavailable"` + `error: "upstream"`, never silently empty. `direction`:
  `from.id === accountId` → `out`; `from.id` present and different → `in`; `from` missing →
  `unknown` (never by username).
- `GET /social/inbox/media?cursor=` → owned media `{ id, caption?, permalink (validated https
  instagram.com only, else omitted), timestamp | null, commentsCount }` via
  `/{accountId}/media?fields=id,caption,permalink,timestamp,comments_count&limit=25`.
- `GET /social/inbox/media/:id/comments?cursor=` → `{ id, text, author: { id?, username? } | null,
  createdAt | null, direction }` via `/{mediaId}/comments?fields=id,text,username,from,timestamp&limit=25`
  (replies to comments are outside coverage and said so).
- Cursors are opaque and sealed: base64url of `{ a: accountId, g: generation, e: edge, id?, after }`
  signed with HMAC-SHA256 (`crypto.subtle`) keyed by `SCOUT_TOKEN` (reuse an existing seal helper
  in this worktree if one exists). A missing/invalid signature, another account, edge or
  generation → 400 `cursor_invalid`; upstream `paging.next` URLs are never accepted or returned;
  the Worker rebuilds every request against the fixed `IG_API` host/version.
- Bounds: one upstream call per request; page sizes as above; text clipped (`clip`, 2,000
  chars); response items capped; errors mapped to the existing codes with tokens/URLs stripped
  (`detail` ≤ 200 chars, never an upstream URL). One surface failing returns its own error only.
- Tests `inboxRead.test.ts` (fake KV + fake fetch as in `replies.test.ts`): no bearer / wrong
  origin → 401/403 with zero upstream fetches; every read path → KV `writes === 0`, zero POST/
  DELETE upstream; both directions + outgoing-only + empty-text + story reply/mention + share +
  unsupported + missing-author rows preserved; two pages with overlapping ids deduplicate on the
  client (server returns raw pages, dedupe tested in `lib/inbox.ts`); malformed, foreign-account
  and foreign-generation cursors → `cursor_invalid`; a hostile `paging.next` host is never
  fetched; second-page upstream failure → first page retained, `coverage: "partial"`; messages ok
  + comments `no_permission` and the reverse; `token_expired`, `rate_limited`, `not_eligible`,
  empty list vs error distinguished; `replies.test.ts` untouched and still green.
- `workers/scout/README.md`: route rows + "read-only, no automation state" note.

**App.**
- `lib/inbox.ts` (+test): zod parsers for the five responses (allowlisted fields only),
  `inboxScope(origin, accountId, kind, id)` key, `mergePages(existing, page)` with id dedupe and
  coverage merge, `providerLink(url)` (https + `instagram.com`/`www.instagram.com` only),

dropped, then DELETEs; resync re-checks fence + `resyncKey` at run time; (2) engagement sample/range = posts with
views > 0; (3) allocation before create, run/cancel never allocate, ambiguous → block, remembered owner first.

**Concerns / deviations (with reasons)**
1. Files beyond the original allowed list, required by the amendments: `lib/digest.ts` + test (Amendment A
   SHA-256; no synchronous digest existed in `lib/`) and `messages/publish.{ar,en}.json` (+3 additive keys
   `publish.jobAmbiguous`, `publish.jobMissing`, `publish.superseded` for the Amendment B block/fence errors; the
   publish namespace is where `usePublish` errors live).
2. Amendment B markers: no new `AutoPostSchema` fields. "Unconfirmed" = `autoPost.jobId` without `sentAt` (sentAt is
   only written after the Worker's reply); "cancelled" = `sentAt`/`jobId` cleared plus the in-memory per-post fence.
   The lifecycle queue and fence are per tab: a resync fired in a second tab concurrently with a cancel in this tab is
   not serialized across tabs (ponytail: Web Locks per post id if that ever shows up).
3. `jobIdFor` blocks whenever another local post claims the id (stricter than "absent on the Worker and ambiguous":
   no Worker list read is made before run/cancel). Fail-closed by design.
4. `ownsJob`: a safe post id counts only for a post that remembers no job id (otherwise "remembered OR safe id" would
   let an alias with its own `-2` job take the generated job; required by the "alias cannot steal" test).
5. `remoteJobs` now also follows a remembered allocation without `sentAt`, so a job committed with a lost reply is not
   shown as another device's job; the retry reuses it.
6. Deals filter is a stage `<select>` instead of an 8-segment `Segmented` (8 Arabic labels overflow a 375 px phone).
7. `app/globals.css` was CRLF in the working tree (index LF); appending made it mixed, so the whole file was normalized
   to LF (git diff shows only the 23 added lines; prettier clean).
8. Estimator defaults (15 SAR / 1000, weights) come from the plan; they are labelled as the owner's assumptions and are
   never exported. The owner may prefer blank defaults.
9. Review routing (Codex queue message) is the planner's step after freeze; not sent by this writer.

**Per finding (RED → fix → GREEN)**
- **R1** RED: `lib/publish.test.ts` `jobOwnership is not a function`; `usePublish.test.ts` "R1: Update schedule and
  the auto-resync…" `expected { ok: true } to deeply equal { ok: false, … }` (POST sent over another post's job). Fix:
  `jobOwnership(post, posts)` → `{ ok: true, jobId } | { ok: false, reason: "ambiguous" | "unallocated" }` (replaces
  `jobIdFor`, same rule). `sendJob` (schedule + auto-resync), `runNow` (before a day is added and again before
  `/run`) and `cancel` all use it; ambiguous → `publish.err.ambiguousOwner`, zero POST/DELETE, neither claimant
  cleared. The Auto-post tab also shows the ambiguity (`autopost-ambiguous`), so a skipped resync is visible. GREEN.
- **R2** RED: store "R2: …" tests `allocatePublishJobId is not a function`; hook "R2: the allocation is in storage
  before the create leaves…" `QuotaExceededError: full` thrown out of `schedule`; "memory-only allocation" storage at
  POST entry `[undefined]`. Fix: store `allocatePublishJobId(postId, jobId)` via `commitFresh` (lock, rehydrate fresh
  storage, missing post never recreated, other remembered id → `conflict`, id held by another post / invalid →
  `taken`) with `persisted = storedJobId(postId) === jobId` read from localStorage; rollback on any miss. `sendJob`
  allocates whenever the job is unconfirmed (no `sentAt`) — also re-proving a remembered id — and sends only after
  `ok`; failure → `publish.err.allocation`, no request. `updatePost` is no longer used for the allocation. Tests cover
  thrown quota, a silent app-key drop, recovery without reload, a post removed in storage, Codex's
  `C`/`C-2`/lost-reply/reload sequence (storage holds the exact id at the fake Worker's create entry; one job). GREEN.
- **R3** RED: hook "R3: an ambiguous receipt…" `markPosted` called once; pure `remoteJobs` `expected [] to deeply
  equal ['J']`. Fix: `jobClaim(jobId, posts)` → `{ owner } | { conflict: [...] } | null` (one remembered owner; two →
  conflict; else a sent post whose safe id it is and which remembers none). `applyJobs` applies results / marked
  posted (and so the Produce quest) only to the owner; `remoteJobs` keeps conflicts; the hub's remote row names the
  claimants (`autopost-remote-conflict`, `publish.conflict`). Both array orders tested. GREEN.
- **R4** RED: hook "R3/R4: the hub read…" `expected undefined to be truthy` (no reconcile); "R4: Discard…"
  `checkAllocation is not a function`; e2e DT-5-R1 case `autopost-unconfirmed` not found (old build). Fix: `applyJobs`
  confirms the owner's unconfirmed allocation the Worker holds (`sentAt`, stage scheduled). Hook gains
  `checkAllocation` / `discardAllocation`, both inside the post's lifecycle queue (no create/resync in flight in this
  tab). Discard re-reads the Worker in the same step: failed read → `publish.unconfirmed.unknown`, kept; id listed →
  confirmed, `publish.unconfirmed.found`, kept (the tab then shows the normal Cancel); absent from a successful read →
  `releasePublishJobId` (commitFresh, exact id, only while unconfirmed). UI `JobNotice` (exported from
  `AutoPostTab.tsx`, also used by the hub's "Allocated, not confirmed" group): Refresh / Retry send / Discard
  allocation; Discard stays disabled until a Refresh read the Worker successfully without the id. Codex's
  clarification test sequence (list fails → refused; list without id → allowed; list with id → confirmed + Cancel) is
  in the hook test and the e2e case. GREEN.
- **R5** RED: jsdom "R5: a form opened before the same backup is restored…" `expected null not to be null` (stale save
  accepted). Fix: `editing.base = businessBase(d)` captured when Edit opens; conflict → `business.deals.err.staleForm`,
  form and typed text kept, stored deal unchanged. GREEN.
- **R6** RED: `lib/businessKit.test.ts` Codex's pair on Oct 17 → `from 2026-10-16, to 2026-10-15`. Fix: range =
  `dayKey(min/max(Date.parse))` over the metric's own sample (engagement keeps the views > 0 sample). GREEN
  (Oct 15 → Oct 16 for avgViews, avgLikes, engagement).
- **R7** RED (old build): e2e `|body.scrollHeight − root| ≤ 2` received `2475.75`; my page-text parser on Codex's
  `dt5-business-print.pdf` / dark → text-show ops per page `[569, 0, 0]`. Fix: print block now `display: none` for

**Concerns / deviations**
1. Scheduling now requires Web Locks (the allocation is a `commitFresh` transaction like CMS/workflow saves). Without
   them `schedule` returns `publish.err.allocation` and sends nothing (fail closed). The hook test file injects the
   queue lock (`setArticlesLock`) in `beforeEach`; Codex's R1 harness must do the same (its README already plans
   "mock only … Web Locks scheduling").
2. Existing assertions changed in form, not strength: the old `jobIdFor` unit test now calls `jobOwnership`
   (`id` → `jobId`, `none` → `unallocated`; every case kept); two hook assertions expect `publish.err.ambiguousOwner`
   instead of the removed `publish.jobAmbiguous` key (renamed per the ruling; AR/EN copy now covers send, run and
   cancel). Codex's quota case expecting a thrown error will see a structured `{ ok: false, error:
   "publish.err.allocation" }` (anticipated in its README).
3. `jobOwnership` follows the ruling literally: a safe-id post that remembers none but whose id another post claims is
   ambiguous (blocked), not suffixed. Unsafe ids (workflow `wf:` posts) still allocate `-2…` when unallocated.
4. "List shows the id → Cancel": the read confirms the allocation (`sentAt`), so the unconfirmed row disappears and
   the tab's normal Cancel takes its place; the hub then lists the post under scheduled (its cancel lives in the tab).
   If the listed id is also claimed by another post, the row shows the ambiguity instead.
5. `applyJobs` confirming an unconfirmed allocation also runs on the watcher / hub reads, not only on Refresh; it only
   ever adds `sentAt` for the single remembered owner of an id the Worker actually lists.
6. `AutoPostScreen.tsx` / `AutoPostTab.tsx` were CRLF in the working tree (index LF, unmodified); normalized to LF
   while editing — `git diff` shows only the R3/R4 additions.
7. The reply template text lives in `lib/businessKit.ts` (generated content in both languages regardless of the UI
   language, like the kit itself); only the UI labels are in `messages/business.*.json`.
8. The e2e clipboard read-back normalizes CRLF (Windows clipboard) before comparing; copy is asserted on desktop only
   (phone emulation has no clipboard permission).
9. Not RED-first: none of the production changes; the `JobNotice` UI's first RED was the e2e case on the old build
   (no jsdom test for the component itself). Cross-tab ordering stays the accepted DT-5 limit (DT-7).

**Concerns / deviations**
1. Beyond the literal ruling, the auto-resync now uses `sentHash` (the ruling's "resync comparison"): an edit made
   while the create POST is out (a pre-R1 window, not only the allocation await) is re-sent after the debounce. A
   "now" send's digest leaves `scheduledAt` out, so a later resync is not triggered just because "now" ≠ the planned
   time; a content edit after Post now re-sends as any edit already did.
2. `publish.superseded` copy widened (AR/EN) to "the post changed or its job was canceled while it was saving. Try
   again." — it now also covers a post removed/changed-id during the allocation. One new key
   `business.reply.earlierSaved` (AR/EN parity).

   non-empty — matching the deployed Worker's own validation; a future Worker field outside `targets` is ignored.

rehydration uses via `PersistedStateSchema.posts` (so `autoPost: AutoPostSchema.optional()`). A failure (missing
post, invalid post, string/null/array/number `autoPost`) is `{ readable: false }`, so `commitJobId`'s `persisted()`
is false and `commitFresh` rolls memory back to the retained id and returns `not-persisted` (the existing
allocation-save error in the UI). Success returns the parsed `autoPost?.jobId`; an absent `autoPost` counts only when
the post itself parses. Legacy optional fields stay compatible because the schema is the one rehydration uses
(defaults fill them). The earlier manual non-string `jobId` check is covered by the schema. Ownership checks, the
allocation path, UI, Business and Worker are untouched.

**Concerns / deviations (with reasons)**
1. Generation is HMAC-SHA256(SCOUT_TOKEN, `gen|accountId|connectedAt ?? issuedAt`) truncated to 32 hex, not a plain
   SHA-256: it lets list routes trust the `account` + `generation` pair without a second `/me` call (one upstream call
   per request) and yields a `409 stale` state after reconnect. Still non-secret input, never the token.
2. List routes take `account` and `generation` query parameters (not in the plan's route list) for the same reason.
3. Client transport is a small own `fetch` in `lib/inbox.ts`, not `call()`: `call()` maps unknown codes to
   `upstream`, which would erase `no_permission`, `not_eligible`, `cursor_invalid` and `stale`.
4. No capability probe call: capabilities come from the granted scopes (or `canReply`); list refusals report the rest.
5. `clip()` keeps only a caption's first line, so message/comment text uses a local multi-line cut at 2,000
   characters (`clip` still used for captions).
6. `share` is only produced if Instagram includes `shares`/`attachments` unasked; no extra fields were requested
   because their Instagram Login contract is unverified. Live history depth, attachment/author fields and access
   eligibility remain unverified release conditions; nothing was deployed.
7. Extra file `components/social/inbox/parts.tsx` (shared StateNote / ListFooter / DirectionChip / When) inside the
   allowed `components/social/inbox/*`.
8. `nav.inbox` lives in `messages/inbox.*.json` (allowed) rather than the base `messages/ar.json`/`en.json`.
9. The `ToolsScreen` "every group" loop narrowed to non-empty groups (see RED evidence); `planned` copy keys and the
   `planned` group type stay for later packets; the unused `planned` readiness helper in `lib/tools.ts` was removed
   (ESLint would flag it).

**Per finding (RED → fix → GREEN)**
1. **6A-1 DraftBox late Discard.** RED: `InboxScreen.test.tsx` "a held Discard keeps text typed after it…" →
   `expected '' to be 'New text typed after Discard'`; e2e `inbox.spec.ts` "a held Discard keeps the text typed after
   it, and that text saves" with the **real** `3z-prod-articles` Web Lock held from the page, against the old served
   build → 2 failed (phone, desktop), `Received: ""`. Fix: `discard` captures the submitted text; on success it sets
   the base to absent and clears only if `textRef.current === submitted`; status `discarded` either way. GREEN: both,
   plus control "a held Discard with unchanged text still clears the editor"; the newer text then saves (`saved`,
   stored text equals it).
2. **6A-2 malformed read-back.** RED (`store/index.test.ts`, failed write then malformed read-back): discard with
   read-back `[]`, `{ invalid: { text: 42 } }`, `{ other: { text, updatedAt } }` (no commitId) and a save whose
   read-back names the attempted commit id in an invalid entry → `4 failed`; unreadable-JSON and the valid-empty
   control already passed. Fix: `storedInboxDrafts` parses `state.inboxDrafts` with `InboxDraftsSchema`
   (`z.record(z.string(), InboxDraftSchema)`, the same schema the persisted root uses); failure → null →
   `not-persisted`, memory rolled back. GREEN: all 6 + "a real discard of the last draft leaves a valid empty
   record, which is proof"; durable storage still holds the draft in every failing case.
3. **6A-3 credential change.** RED (`useInbox.test.ts`): "a token change clears the view at once…" → `expected
   { accountId: 'A', … } to be null`; "a held old-token account answer is dropped…" → same; screen test "hides the
   old account's conversations as soon as the token changes" (run against the snapshot `useInbox.ts` copied in,
   then restored) → `not to contain 'fan_one'`. Fix: module-private `epoch` bumped by a `useStore.subscribe` when
   `scoutUrl`/`scoutToken` change, which also `resetInbox()`s (account, lists, selection, busy gone at once;
   `accountSeq` bumped); `epoch` is in the list fence and checked after the account read. Memory only; draft scopes
   unchanged (origin + account id + kind + id) — test "draft scopes carry the origin and account id, never the
   token". GREEN.
4. **6A-4 A → B → A.** RED: "Worker A → B → A…" and "an account switch and back (same Worker)…" → `expected
   [ 'A-old' ] to deeply equal [ 'A-new' ]`. Fix: acceptance also requires `now.busy[key] === token` (the request is
   still its list's current session; any reset or newer read replaced it). GREEN (busy all released).
5. **6A-5 response identity.** RED: `lib/inbox.test.ts` "refuses a page whose account or generation is not the one
   asked for, on every list" and `useInbox.test.ts` "a page bearing another account / generation is refused as
   stale…" → foreign rows merged. Fix: `getPage` (the one function all four list calls route through) returns
   `{ ok: false, error: { code: "stale" } }` on mismatch; `mergeFailure` keeps existing rows (`partial`, `next`
   kept) or shows `unavailable`. GREEN.
6. **6A-6 malformed 200.** RED (`inboxRead.test.ts`): conversations/media/comments with `{}`, `data: "nope"`,
   `data: {0:"x"}`, `data: null`, and messages with `messages: {}` / non-array data → 200 `end`. Fix: `page()`
   throws `SocialError("upstream")` unless `data` is an array (→ `unavailable` first page, `partial` with a cursor).
   GREEN; `data: []` stays 200 `end` in each case.
7. **6A-7 missing metadata.** RED: rows missing only `from` / only `created_time` / text-story-unsupported rows with
   neither → 502 `history_unavailable`. Fix: `history_unavailable` only when every listed row is bare (none of
   `from`, `created_time`, `message`, `story`, `is_unsupported`) or there is no messages edge. GREEN; bare-id control
   still 502 `history_unavailable`; a bare + real mix keeps both rows.
8. **6A-8 cursor bounds.** RED: 1,000-char `after` on conversations and on a 256-char conversation id → `more` with
   an over-long `next`. Fix: `seal` returns null when the sealed cursor exceeds `CURSOR_MAX` (1,500) → `coverage:
   "cap"`, `next: null`. GREEN; control "the longest cursor it does emit opens on the next call" (binary-searched to
   the 1,500 limit) passes and the same cursor is still refused on another edge with zero calls.
9. **6A-9 byte budget.** RED: 2 MiB streamed page (no Content-Length), 1 MiB later page with a lying
   `Content-Length: 10`, 512 KiB `/me`, 2,100-char permalink → all accepted. Fix: reader-local `boundedJson`
   (`inboxRead.ts`; `http.ts` untouched): budgeted fetch, body read through `getReader()` with a byte counter,
   `cancel()` and `upstream` past `PAGE_BYTES_MAX = 256 KiB` before any `JSON.parse`; `instagramLink` drops input or
   normalised output over 2,048 chars. GREEN: pulled ≤ 256 KiB + one 64 KiB chunk, `unavailable`/`partial`, a 200 KiB
   page still reads, a 2,048-char permalink kept. Budget documented in README "Inbox reads" and `36-inbox.md`.

**Concerns / deviations**
1. Finding 8 uses the existing coverage value **`cap`** (documented since DT-6A as "a local limit; more may exist")
   instead of a new `"local_cap"` string: a synonym would widen the Worker/client contract (`COVERAGES`, footer copy)
   for the same meaning. Codex's W3 probe therefore still fails its `more` branch by design (see above). If Fable
   wants the literal `local_cap`, it is a two-line Worker/client change plus copy.
2. The epoch subscription lives at module level in `useInbox.ts` (runs once on import, client and prerender alike);
   any `apiKeys` URL/token change — Settings edit, import, reset — clears the in-memory inbox view, which is the
   ruling's intent. The screen's existing effect then re-reads.

  `history_unavailable` only when every row `isRow && bareRow`; otherwise it goes to `page()`, which fails it as
  malformed. Applies to conversations, `messages.data`, media and comments through the one shared `page()`.

  `{id:null}`, `null`, `"row"`, an array row) → first 502 unavailable / later 502 partial, no items, per edge;
  a bad row after a full page is unavailable, never `cap`; genuine `data: []` → 200 `end`; minimal valid rows
  (`{id}` / `{id, message}`) map with unknown labels (`updatedAt`/`createdAt`/`timestamp: null`,
  `direction: "unknown"`, `from`/`author: null`).

**Concerns / deviations (with reasons).**
1. No helper extraction: `inboxReadCommon.ts` repeats the small private helpers of `inboxRead.ts` (sealing,
   bounded transport, row checks, Meta failure mapping) instead of extracting them, so the accepted Instagram
   reader and its tests stay byte-identical (allowed fallback in the plan).
2. YouTube account call uses `part=id,snippet,contentDetails` (plan: `id,snippet`) so the uploads playlist id comes
   in the same single call; the uploads id travels only inside the sealed `uploads` ref.
3. Below-item routes take the sealed ref as the path segment (`posts/:ref/replies`, `videos/:ref/threads`,
   `comments/:ref/replies`) and videos take `?uploads=<ref>`: the plan's `:id` is the ref, so a bare id is refused.
4. The optional read-scope connect option (`threads_read_replies`) was not added: Threads' `exchange` records the
   configured scope string, so an honest option would also need it to record granted scopes (a sync/auth change
   outside B1). The Threads replies state therefore shows no Settings link. Until a reviewed change adds that scope,
   live Threads replies will stay `no_permission`.
5. YouTube access tokens last an hour and only the analytics sync refreshes them; the reader never does, so the
   honest live state between syncs is often `token_expired` ("sync or reconnect, then Refresh"). A dedicated,
   reviewed refresh path would be a later decision, not part of a pure reader.
6. Provider hook tests live in a new `useProviderInbox.test.ts` (plan named `useInbox.test.ts`) to keep
   `useInbox.*` untouched; hook-before-test order and the store canaries passing at once are noted above.
7. A provider switch clears every comment-provider list session (A → B → A safe); Instagram's own reads live in the
   untouched `useInbox` store and keep their DT-6A fences (its identity does not change on a switch).
8. Live Threads/YouTube coverage (nested depth, hidden/pending replies, production eligibility, embedded-reply
   counts) is unverified; synthetic fixtures only. DT-6B-2 reviewed sending remains required.

**Per finding (RED → fix → GREEN).**
- **B1-1 seal key.** RED: in `inboxReadThreads.test.ts` / `inboxReadYouTube.test.ts`, an independent WebCrypto
  client (no product helper) holding the bearer and the account route's real generation forged post / video /
  comment / uploads refs and a cursor under three bearer-derived keys (the DT-6B-1 scheme, the raw bearer, the R1
  derivation over the bearer): answers were 502/200 after an upstream GET (want 400 before any call); missing /
  short / bearer-equal secrets answered 200 (want 503); an echoed provider message leaked the secret. Fix:
  `inboxReadCommon.ts` derives a per-provider key `HMAC-SHA256(INBOX_SEAL_SECRET, "inbox-seal-v1|<provider>")` for
  generations, cursors and refs (`openRef` / `openCursorV2` now take the provider); `routes.ts` passes
  `env.INBOX_SEAL_SECRET` only when present, ≥ 32 characters and not equal to `SCOUT_TOKEN`, else `undefined`, so
  every Threads/YouTube route (account included: it mints the generation and uploads ref) is `503 not_configured`
  before any token read or call; `failureOf` also cuts the secret from echoed details. The dashboard names the setting
  (`inbox.state.{threads,youtube}.not_configured`, `not_configured` added to the provider-worded codes; RED first:
  1 failing view test). README "Configuration" row + "Seal key" paragraph (owner sets it in Cloudflare Variables and
  Secrets; not a repository secret). Instagram's DT-6A reader and seals untouched. GREEN: forged refs/cursors 400 /
  `cursor_invalid` with zero fetch, genuine listing refs open, secret absent from every answer.
- **B1-2 channel envelope.** RED: `{}`, `{items:null}`, `true`, `[]` → 200 empty pick. Fix: `googleBody` accepts a 200
  only with a JSON object body; the account route requires `Array.isArray(items)` → else `502 upstream`. GREEN; `{items:
  []}` still the honest no-channel answer, two channels still `needsSelection`. The DT-6B-1 assertion that used `{}` as
  "none" encoded this bug: it now uses `{ items: [] }` (comment in place), and `{}` is asserted upstream in the new block.
- **B1-3 reply totals.** RED: missing / null / "garbage" / "3" / -1 / 1.5 → `totalReplyCount: 0`; parser rejected null;
  the view hid Load replies. Fix: Worker emits `null` unless a non-negative safe integer; `lib/inbox.ts`
  `totalReplyCount: number | null` (strict int ≥ 0 otherwise); `ProviderView` offers Load replies when the total is
  unknown or above the embedded count, the subset line only with a known total; valid 0 shows neither. The wire field
  keeps the name `totalReplyCount` (the ruling's "totalReplies" wording) so no existing assertion or e2e changed.
- **B1-4 id grammar.** RED: Threads `{id:123.5}`, `2**53`, `-0.5`, `1e21`, booleans/null, a fractional reply id, and
  YouTube fractional/unsafe video, top-level and embedded reply ids were accepted. Fix: `plainId` accepts a string
  matching the grammar or a JSON safe integer whose decimal string matches it; the row check uses it, so such a row
  fails the whole page (`upstream` / `unavailable`). GREEN incl. round trips: `90001`, `"90002"`, `"a-b_c"` posts and a
  numeric video id `4242` each mint a ref that the reader's own replies/threads route accepts (one GET).

  answer neither blocks nor releases"): the old busy token blocked the return visit and its late answer landed.

  included; video also ends its reply sessions; another channel ends every YouTube session), so a late answer fails the
  `busy[key] === token` fence and its token-checked release is a no-op. Completed rows stay (control: P → Q → P with P
  read shows its rows, one GET).
- **B1-6 provider visits.** RED: a held account answer released after leaving started a hidden posts read; return with a
  held selected view left it empty. Fix: a module `visit` counter bumped on every switch; `loadAccount`, `openProvider`
  and `refreshProvider` stop when it changed; a switch also clears `accountBusy`; back on a provider, a selected post /
  video whose list never landed returns to the first list (ruling), first list loaded if needed. Control: a loaded
  selected video survives Instagram → YouTube with no request.
- **B1-7 refresh.** RED: after Refresh the old `[R(old), gone]` reply list survived over fresh embedded `[R(fresh)]`,
  total 1. Fix: Refresh on a selected video drops the reply lists and in-flight reply sessions of every comment in that
  video's thread list, then refreshes the threads; replies reload only on Load replies. GREEN: edits, deletion, count
  change, a held old reply page released after a second Refresh never lands; drafts identical (control test, passes
  before and after); unchanged replies control.

  end/failure had no own footer. Fix: `ibx-yt-replies-footer` under each loaded comment (`data-coverage`): `end` "all
  the replies YouTube returned for this comment", `cap` the local-limit line, `partial` its own line, plus the state
  note; the button is Load more with a cursor, Retry after a failure without one. The thread list's end line now reads

**Root cause.** `loadList` returned early when its list already had a session (`if (s.busy[key]) return;`), so a
second accepted Refresh (or any new read of that list) was dropped and the older request kept the only valid token.

**Fix (one shared place, every caller routes through it).** `useProviderInbox.ts`: the early return is removed. Every
read of a list takes a new token (`busy[key] = ++requestSeq`) at once and asks again; the existing fence
(`busy[key] === token` + epoch/origin/account/generation/selection) then orphans the older request — its success or
error neither replaces rows nor releases busy (token-checked release is a no-op). Busy follows the newest read; the
Refresh button (`InboxScreen.tsx`, disabled only while the account check runs) stays enabled and is now never silently
skipped. Navigation (`selectVideo`/`selectPost`/`selectChannel` end sessions) and provider switch (`busy: {}`, visit
token) drop both requests, unchanged. R1's reply-cache invalidation on Refresh, drafts, rows on failure
(`mergeFailure`), per-comment footers and on-demand replies are untouched. Doc comments updated. `InboxScreen.tsx`,
`InboxScreen.test.tsx`, `ProviderView.tsx`, messages: not needed, byte-identical.

**What it does.** Prepare → review → explicit Send → durable receipt, as planned: SQLite Durable Object
`SendCoordinator` per `youtube|<channel>` (prepare idempotent by operation id + payload, convergence on the live
submission key through a partial unique index, `claim` one `UPDATE … WHERE state='prepared' RETURNING`, `settle` once,
`cancel` prepared only, 90-day purge of settled rows with tombstones, `dispatching`/`unknown` never purged or
re-claimable, no network inside). Routes under `/social/inbox/youtube/send/*` with the force-ssl / live-token / sealed
`send-target-v1|youtube` / text / ONE preflight GET checks and distinct codes; confirm claims before the one
`comments.insert` POST (15 s abort, 256 KB bounded answer) and classifies sent / rejected / unknown with no retry.
Reads add `sendRef` (threads), parent `sendRef` + `replyParentNote` (embedded replies) and
`capabilities.sendComments`; still pure GETs. App: persisted `inboxSendOps` (cap 50, settled dropped first,
`commitFresh` + read-back, fence on the expected operation id, no text), handle written before prepare and set to
`dispatching` before confirm, fenced views (epoch, scope session, channel + generation → "closed"), `SendReview`
sheet with every state, EN/AR copy, Save/Copy/Discard unchanged.

external for the lazily loaded MCP path), and proves: prepare idempotency/conflict/convergence, three concurrent claims
→ exactly one `claimed`, two concurrent settles → one, persistence of a claim and a receipt across a disposed and
recreated runtime on the same on-disk storage (new stub, same id), purge + tombstone blocking id and submission, and
through the Worker routes with a fake Google outbound: prepare → two concurrent confirms → one `comments.insert` with
the exact body → restart → status `sent` and a repeated confirm without a second POST.

**Deviations / concerns.**
1. Runtime proof uses Miniflare from the pinned Wrangler instead of pool-workers (above); Codex may still want the
   pool-workers config once a download is allowed.
2. Confirm takes `{ operationId, digest, account }`, and status/cancel take `account` (query/body): the account is
   needed to address the per-account coordinator. The plan listed `{ operationId, digest }`.
3. Confirm re-checks grant, token, generation, digest and expiry but makes no second preflight GET (as the plan's
   confirm step lists); a comment deleted inside the 10-minute review is refused by Google → `rejected`.
4. Extra codes beyond the plan's list: `text_invalid`, `conflict`, `receipt_unavailable` (coordinator unreachable before
   the claim), plus the existing `stale`, `rate_limited`, `upstream`, `not_connected`.
5. Three existing exact assertions in `inboxReadYouTube.test.ts` were extended with the new additive fields
   (`sendComments: "no_permission"`, `sendRef`, the reply's `sendRef` + `replyParentNote`); nothing removed or loosened.
6. `store.ts`, `index.ts` and `wrangler.jsonc` were CRLF on disk (autocrlf) and failed Prettier; they are now LF. Git's
   content diff is unaffected (only the intended lines show).
7. `workers/scout/README.md` is not Prettier-clean at baseline (wide tables elsewhere), so it is excluded from the
   Prettier check; the new section follows the file's style.
8. The e2e fake Worker now allows POST in CORS and passes the parsed body to handlers; every older test still asserts
   no non-GET request.
9. YouTube coverage note copy (EN/AR) now says nothing is sent unless the owner reviews and presses Send;
   `inbox.sub` ("read-only") was left unchanged.
10. Known ceilings (marked in docs): an unknown/dispatching operation blocks new sends on that comment on this device
    (no dismiss); tombstones are never purged; `capabilities.sendComments` is scope-only (a missing binding shows at
    prepare as `not_configured`/`receipt-store`); a Worker without `sendComments` shows no send UI.
11. Readiness still open: the YouTube connect flow does not request `youtube.force-ssl`, so live sending stays
    `no_permission`; the Durable Object binding/migration is local only (never provisioned or deployed).

**Deviations / concerns.**
1. The e2e fake Worker's `sendIntent` answered a constant digest (`"a"×64`) and revision (`"rev"`); with 2A-4 binding the
   client correctly refuses that, so the fixture now answers like the real Worker (SHA-256 of the exact text, the draft
   revision it was given). No assertion was removed or loosened; the three existing DT-6B-2A cases pass unchanged.
2. `receiptVersion` is the Worker intent's `updatedAt` in ms. Claim and settle share one request timestamp, so equal
   versions are ordered by the state rules (settled final, unknown only settles); a Worker `prepared` may replace a
   local `dispatching` mark of equal version (benign: the coordinator still claims once).
3. `resetSendViews()` now bumps the global epoch (a pending answer lands as `closed`) instead of every session; the
   connection-change subscription calls it.
4. A failed cancel is shown in the draft box (the sheet has closed by then); Check status is the reopened sheet, which
   reads the same operation. Error-phase sheets show Check status whenever a handle exists.
5. Answers whose durable record is refused as `stale` (another tab recorded newer proof) are still shown in the tab
   that asked (newest action only); storage keeps the newer proof.
6. Store test helper `set()` parameter type widened from `ReturnType<typeof op>` to the action's handle type so tests can
   pass `receiptVersion`; no assertion changed.
7. New copy (EN/AR, parity test green): `inbox.send.parent`, `parentNotLoaded`, `parentId`, `openParent`,
   `why.mismatch`, `why.lookup`, `err.capacity`, `err.cancelFailed`, `err.clearFailed`.

**Interpretations and deviations (for review).**
1. *Direct reply, strictly.* The plan grants a `sendRef` when `root_post.id` is the owned post and `replied_to.id` is
   known; this requires `replied_to.id` to equal the owned post as well (a nested reply gets none), and the preflight
   checks id, `root_post.id` and `replied_to.id`. Stricter than written, matching "exact direct reply".
2. *Resume from `created`.* The 10-minute review deadline governs `prepared` only. A confirm on `created` re-checks
   token, gate, generation and the exact digest (a fresh explicit confirmation of the same immutable text) but not the
   original deadline; otherwise a durable container would be stuck forever, since convergence returns it to any new
   operation for the same submission.
3. *Crash leaves `creating`/`publishing`, not `unknown_*`.* No lease or timer may move them (contract); status reports
   the in-flight stage and nothing reclaims it. 2B-2 must present both as "may have happened, check Threads".
4. *Receipt failure after a provider success.* The route tries to settle the matching unknown state durably; if that
   also fails it answers `unknown_creation`/`unknown_publication` with `unknownReason: "receipt"` and the durable row
   stays `creating`/`publishing` (never claimable). If the container receipt actually committed but its reply was lost,
   the settle finds `created` and the next confirm publishes once.
5. *Runtime protocol entry.* Because production eligibility is not injectable through `src/index.ts` (by design), the
   route matrix runs a test-only bundle (esbuild stdin inside the test, never shipped, no env flag, no browser path)
   that calls the same handler with `{ ok: true }`. Its `FAIL_OPS` binding exists only in that test runtime.
6. *Points not separately injectable through the route:* a crash between the create claim and the POST leaving the
   Worker, and between the container commit and the publish claim. Their durable states (`creating` with no POST;
   `created`) are covered by the coordinator restart tests, the publish-claim storage failure row and the unit resume
   tests.
7. *Reuse.* `BODY_BYTES_MAX`, `POST_TIMEOUT_MS`, `REVIEW_MS` and `Reply` are imported from the pinned
   `inboxSendYouTube.ts` (import only). Its private `readCapped`, `sha256Hex` and send-key derivation are repeated
   (~40 lines) because that file is pinned and does not export them.
8. *Existing assertions extended, not weakened:* `inboxReadThreads.test.ts` capability expectations now include
   `sendReplies: "permission_unverified"`, and the two direct-reply rows of the existing listing case now require a
   `sendRef` (the nested row requires none). Prettier was applied to that file.
9. Refusal codes are `meta_<code>` (else `http_<status>`); unknown states stay in the convergence set, so a new
   operation id for the same submission returns the uncertain intent instead of a fresh one. Column
   `created_at_provider` is exposed as `containerRecordedAt`.

**Readiness gap (unchanged by this packet).** Production preparation is closed (`permission_unverified`): the
endpoint-specific permission for creating a Threads reply and a trusted grant-provenance contract are unverified
(Meta permission pages 429 in Codex's audit; the collection-level scope list is not a minimum; `threads.ts` stores the
configured `TH_SCOPES`, not the grant). The 500-code-point cap is local policy. Container-status reconciliation
(GET-only, explicit) is a follow-up. `THREADS_SEND_COORDINATOR` / `v2-threads-send` are local only. UI (2B-2) and
connection readiness remain required; this packet does not complete Threads sending.

**Deviations (recorded rulings of the executor; Codex to judge).**
1. *Local Confirm mark.* The handle has two local states: `preparing` (before Prepare, as YouTube) and `confirming`
   (before Confirm/Resume: the request may have left). A reload or failed lookup on `confirming` shows the distinct
   local-uncertainty view `uncertain` with Check status only; durable `creating/publishing/unknown_*` keep their own
   copy. `confirming` stands for the receipt it was marked on (`created` when a container id is stored, else
   `prepared`) in the CAS.
2. *Handle fields.* Beyond the plan's list the handle keeps `account` (needed for the credential-independent
   `GET …/send/:op?account=`) and `commitId` (read-back proof), as YouTube's. The schema is strict (an extra key such
   as `text` is `invalid`).
3. *Excerpts by id from memory.* The review takes the root post's text/permalink and the receiving reply's text from
   the in-memory Threads lists by the intent's `rootPostId` / `replyToId` (never from the target, never persisted);
   missing rows show the ids only. The root link is the post's existing `threadsLink`-validated permalink.
4. *Wire capture in the unit file.* Fixtures are captured live in `lib/inboxThreadsSend.test.ts` (computed-path
   imports of `scout`, `social/store`, `social/inboxSendThreads`, `social/threadsSendCoordinator`, node:sqlite), not
   copied JSON and not a separate wire file; `lib/inbox.wire.test.ts` stays pinned.
5. *Parser strictness.* `containerId` is required for `created/publishing/published`, forbidden for
   `prepared/creating/cancelled/expired/unknown_creation`, optional for `rejected` (publish-stage refusals carry it)
   and `unknown_publication`; `publishedId` / `failureCode`+`failureDetail` / `unknownReason` only on their own state.
6. *Uncertain confirm codes.* `network`, `upstream`, `auth`, `mismatch`, `receipt_unavailable` keep the `confirming`
   mark (status only); every other Worker code is refused before any claim and rolls the mark back.
7. *Readiness function.* `threadsSendReadiness()` (in `lib/inboxThreadsSend.ts`) takes no input and returns the
   closed literal; tests replace it with `vi.mock`. The account capability only decides whether the opener appears
   (absent = older Worker), never whether sending is ready.

**Concerns.**
- Check status needs the Threads account answer on screen to equal the handle's account (fence). While the account
  read fails or another Threads account is connected, handles are kept but cannot be checked from this device.
- Check status for a row lives inside its draft box (opened by "Draft", as YouTube); the Threads view's recovery list
  ("Threads replies to check") is the always-visible path and lists every handle of the account, so a scope can appear
  twice (list and open draft box) sharing one view.
- Closing the sheet on a settled state (published, rejected, expired, cancelled) finishes and removes the handle, as
  YouTube does; a published handle seen only in the recovery list is acknowledged by closing it.
- The enabled path (Prepare/Send/Resume) is exercised only by module mocks; no browser run of it exists by design.
- Readiness gap unchanged: production Threads sending closed (`permission_unverified`); endpoint permission and
  trusted grant provenance unverified; 500-code-point cap local policy; container reconciliation deferred.

- **2B2-1 immutable publishedId.** `ThreadsExpect.publishedId` + `bindThreadsIntent` binds container and publication
  ids alike (`PROOFS`); `expectOf` carries the stored `publishedId`; `threadsSendStep` refuses another container or
  publication id (`stale`) and another `account` / `draftRevision` / `digest` / `workerOrigin` (`invalid`) for the same
  operation at any version; a mismatching status answer now shows the last durable view (`error` + `mismatch` + the

  storage after `commitFresh` returned (outside the lock), so a writer that lands after the transaction is seen. The
  hook's `committed()` requires `current` = the answer's operation id, `receiptVersion` and state before `show`, in
  `settle` (status, Send/Resume, Cancel) and canonical Prepare; otherwise `reconcile` → superseded + Check status.
  RED: store "R1: a write answers with the handle stored after its commit…" and hook "Check status shows its answer
  only…" / "canonical Prepare opens its review only…" failed; Codex client race ×2 failed. GREEN all.

  write from the action's captured connection and kept by the store through steps that omit it. `threadsOpOrigin()` =
  recorded origin, else the scope key's origin. `checkThreadsReply` captures a status-only fence (epoch, visit,
  provider = threads, same URL + token; no account/generation), refuses (zero requests, `closed`) unless the handle's
  origin equals the configured one, and asks `GET …/send/:op?account=<stored account>`. Send/Resume/Cancel also refuse

**Deviations (Codex to judge).**
1. *Legacy origin.* The ruling says handles without `workerOrigin` are "treated as the current origin on first read and
   rewritten once". I use the origin in the handle's v2 scope key instead: same result when the scope's origin is the
   current one, and it never retargets an old handle to a new Worker, which the review forbids. No separate rewrite on
   read (a render-time write); the next durable write (e.g. the first status answer) records it.
2. *Expiry key.* The once-guard keys on `scope|operationId`, not `(operationId, reviewExpiresAt)`: an operation's
   deadline is immutable on the Worker, so this is the same in correct cases, and it also stops a loop when malformed
   answers name a new past deadline each time (found by my first e2e fake). It is page-memory: reopening the sheet
   later does not auto-check again; Check status stays manual.
3. *`current` from storage.* `current` is read from the shared storage after the commit returned (outside the lock),
   so another tab's write is seen; unreadable storage gives `null` → the view reconciles (superseded) instead of
   showing the answer.
4. *Status mismatch view.* A status answer that fails binding now shows the last durable view (`lastKnown`) with the
   mismatch error and the stored status line, instead of the local "uncertain" view (wrong copy for a published
   handle). Local marks (`preparing`/`confirming`) still show "uncertain".
5. *Answers after a Worker URL change.* A status answer from the handle's own Worker that arrives after the URL changed
   may still be recorded (genuine proof, from the Worker it was asked of) but its view is `closed`; nothing more is
   asked. Unchanged from 2B-2.
6. *Two assertions changed by the 2B2-3 ruling* (not weakened, inverted by it): hook "checking from another account
   than the handle's asks nothing" → "…asks the handle's own account, once" (one exact GET asserted; the zero-request
   rule moved to the another-Worker test); component recovery list "of the account on screen" → "of this Worker"
   (2 items, `account=25` asserted).
7. *Separate foreign section.* Another Worker's handles render in `ibx-ths-recovery-foreign`, so the checkable
   `ibx-ths-recovery` stays absent for them (Codex's worker-switch control asserts that and still passes).

**Concerns.**
- Cancel keeps the 2B-2 loaded-account fence: from the recovery list with an account error or another account, the
  Cancel button of a prepared review shows `closed` (Check status works). The ruling scopes recovery to status only.
- A process slip, fixed before any check counted: one scripted test-file splice dropped the existing "cancel and
  finish" describe of `useThreadsSend.test.ts`; it was restored byte-for-byte from Codex's snapshot (diff against the
  snapshot: only the two ruling lines above removed). A mutation run that hung was stopped, its source restored from
  its backup (prettier/eslint clean), and its orphaned vitest processes ended.
- The handoff's owner line still names this writer; Fable sets owner none at freeze. Readiness gap unchanged:
  production Threads sending closed (`permission_unverified`), endpoint permission and grant provenance unverified,
  500-code-point cap local policy, container reconciliation deferred.

### DT-6B-2C-1 implementation record (Opus 5.5, 17 Oct 2026)

Single writer, Worker only, in the managed worktree (`codex/discover-inspiration`, HEAD `0e1fdb0`). No commit, stash,
reset, push, deploy, provisioning, secret, live provider call, app build or :3000 restart. Fake transport only.

**Files.** New: `workers/scout/src/social/instagramPublicSendCoordinator.ts` (+ `.test.ts`, `.runtime.test.ts`),
`instagramPublicSend.ts` (+ `.test.ts`), `inboxSendInstagram.ts` (+ `.test.ts`). Edited: `replies.ts` (imports,
`ReplyLogEntry.error` type widened by `"not_configured"`, `PollDeps.publicClaim`, and the `if (dmSent && pub &&
http.budget.ok)` block only), `replies.test.ts` (harness: every `makeEnv` gets the real coordinator over node:sqlite;
11 new cases appended; no existing assertion touched), `routes.ts` (narrow `instagram/send` dispatch + header line),
`store.ts` (env field), `src/index.ts` (third named export + amended comment), `wrangler.jsonc` (binding
`INSTAGRAM_PUBLIC_SEND_COORDINATOR`, migration `v3-instagram-public-send`), `sendCoordinator.runtime.test.ts` and
`threadsSendCoordinator.runtime.test.ts` (binding/migration lists; the Threads test entry also exports the third
class, which Miniflare needs for the wrangler binding list), Worker README, `planning/tools/37-inbox-send.md`, this
handoff.

**What was built.**
- Coordinator: one SQLite DO per `instagram|<user_id>` with `intents`, `public_effects (account, comment_id) PK`,
  `tombstones`. `claimConfirm` is one `transactionSync`: `UPDATE … WHERE state='prepared' RETURNING`, then
  `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING`; a held (or tombstoned) effect makes the intent `already_claimed`
  (`failureDetail` automatic/manual/retired, one version step), zero POST. `claimAuto` is the same insert; the loser
  gets the row. `settle` once by the claiming actor, mirrored into the manual intent. `cancel` prepared-only. Claimed
  and unknown effects never expire/purge; finished rows purge after 90 days into tombstones (op, sent submission,
  effect). No network inside.
- Shared helper: `dispatchPublicReply` (POST `/{comment}/replies` form `{message, access_token}`, budget take, 15 s
  abort, `PAGE_BYTES_MAX` streaming read, string `id` → sent, 4xx Meta error body → rejected + reply for the caller's
  mapping, timeout/network/5xx/malformed/contradictory/oversize → unknown; no retry, no substitution);
  `verifyTarget` (≤ 3 `boundedJson` GETs, `/me` `user_id` identity, first media page and first comment page with
  `limit=IG_VERIFY_PAGE` (50), exact `isRow`/`plainId` membership, absent → `target_unverified` /
  `outside-local-window`, malformed → upstream, never `paging.next`); `publicEffects(ns)` client (null without a
  binding; throws on any failure).
- Routes: `instagramSendHandler({ fetch, now, eligibility })`, default `permission_unverified` → `403 no_permission`
  before any provider call. Token + stamp captured once; re-read after the GETs and immediately before the claim
  (`409 stale` / `reconnected`). Status/cancel: bearer + stored operation, zero provider calls. Missing binding →
  `503 not_configured` / `receipt-store`. Streaming 16,384-byte body budget. Token and seal scrubbed.
- `replies.ts`: claim via `deps.publicClaim ?? publicEffects(env.INSTAGRAM_PUBLIC_SEND_COORDINATOR)` before the POST;
  missing/unreadable → `publicReply: "failed"`, `error ??= "not_configured"`, `detail: "public-claim-store"`, no POST;
  lost → `"skipped"`, `detail: "already_claimed"`; won → shared helper with exact `fill(pub, username)`, then settle;
  sent counts only with a durable receipt; rejected runs `graph` on Meta's reply (codes and stop policy unchanged);
  unknown or lost receipt → `"failed"`, `error ??= "upstream"`, `detail: "unknown-delivery"`.

   accepted 2C-1 SQL (no row LIMIT): it is bounded by frequency, not batch size. A purge failure now also fails the
   automatic claim/settle call that triggered it (fail closed: no POST, or `unknown-delivery`).

   refresh that changes `expiresAt`) is `stale` until the next request.

   accepted converge rule returns the canonical operation.

**Deviations / concerns.**
1. Prepare now binds `generation` and `mediaId` too (ruling A). The coordinator's convergence key is account/revision/
   comment/digest, so a live intent for the same submission prepared under an older connection (another generation)
   or another media answers `receipt_unavailable` instead of converging. Fail closed; the owner cancels or waits for
   that intent to expire. Not observed in any existing test.
2. The validator checks `text` as a non-empty string and `digest` by shape; it does not recompute `sha256(text)` against
   `digest` (the phase bindings already pin both to the reviewed values).
3. `generation` is checked as a non-empty string, not the 32-hex shape `generationOf` produces (bound by equality at
   prepare and claim anyway).
4. A manual answer carrying `error` beside other fields is now `receipt_unavailable` at prepare/status/cancel/claim
   even when the error is one of conflict/not_found/bad_request (previously mapped to that error). Pure envelopes keep
   the mapping.
5. The handoff's owner line still names this writer; the freeze/owner-none flip is the planner's step.

**Design as built (deviations marked).**
- Coordinator: tables `conversations`, `effects` (PK account, conversation, inbound message), `default_cooldown`,
  `tombstones`, `meta`; `claim` / `settle` / `takeover` / `resume` / `status` exactly per the plan. Deviation 1: the
  takeover block applies to `auto:*` actors only; a `manual:*` claim (the person's own send, internal only) is allowed
  in a `human` conversation (a literal "refuse any claim while human" would make the next packet's manual send
  impossible after takeover). `isDefault` must equal `actor === "auto:default"`. Takeover/resume on the current
  revision with the mode already set is a no-op (`changed: false`, no bump).
- Send helper `instagramDm(ns, { now, secret }).claimAndSend(http, attempt)`: SHA-256 of the exact JSON body is the
  payload digest; claim → validated (`claimResult`: error-free, conversation identity, full effect identity incl.
  recipient/actor/digest/generation/state/integer version; `blocked_by_takeover` only for auto with mode human;
  `cooldown` only for the default) → ONE POST (`replyCore.sendReply`'s exact `{ id }` body and headers,
  `redirect: "manual"`, 15 s, 256 KB streaming) → settle validated (`recordsDm`). A lost receipt after a typed refusal
  stays `rejected` (nothing was sent; the effect stays `claimed`, cooldown reserved). `dmTick` builds the tick's
  authority: fresh `/me?fields=user_id` (reused when the poll fetched `/me` that tick), status stamp, generation
  `sha256("ig-dm-gen|account|stamp")[:32]`, the fence (token+status together, token again; fresh clock; expiry).
- `answerInbox`: per answered item, budget check `left < DM_SUBREQUESTS (3)`; malformed ids → `skipped`/`unavailable`;
  no sender → `not_configured`/`dm-claim-store`; `dm.account !== igUserId` → `not_configured`/`dm-account`
  (deviation 2: extra detail for the ambiguous-account case); fence failure → logged, `failures`+1, tick stops, nothing
  recorded; fresh-clock window miss → silent, handled; then the outcome table in tool 37. Pre-claim failures
  (`dm-claim-store`, `dm-account`) use the existing `MAX_RETRIES` counter and stop the DMs for the tick with
  `{ upstream, <detail> }` (deviation 3: bounded retry instead of permanent give-up or per-tick write storms).
  Deviation 4: `ReplyLogEntry.dm` gains `"skipped"` (already_claimed / takeover / unavailable); the pinned dashboard
  renders it with its "failed" words, not red, until the UI packet. Unknown delivery leaves `sends`/`failures`
  untouched (as the public branch).
- `replies.ts`: `PollDeps.clock` (default `now` + real elapsed time); `fetchedThisTick` flag before the existing `/me`
  branch; in the DM read's `try`, when `inboxSince` exists, `dmTick(...)` then `inbox.igUserId = dm.account;
  inbox.dm = dm` (the conversations are read with the fresh account; a `/me` failure is a failed read). Header line and
  the `REPLY_CAP` comment updated; `ReplyLogEntry` doc/type as above. The comment-answer loop including the accepted

**workerd matrix (`instagramDmCoordinator.runtime.test.ts`, 14 cases, every POST counted).**

| Case                                                                  | Result                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| real entry: 4 classes; 2 polls + manual + other auto on one event     | 1 `claimed`, 3 `already_claimed`; other account / conversation / later turn each claimable |
| takeover after a claim (two concurrent CAS at rev 0)                  | one wins, one `conflict`; `inFlight` = the claimed effect; next auto `blocked_by_takeover` |
| stale resume, explicit resume                                         | `conflict`; then auto rev 2; the claimed effect stays `already_claimed` (claimed)          |
| takeover before a claim                                               | `blocked_by_takeover`                                                                      |
| 3 concurrent default claims, one person, different events             | `claimed`, `cooldown`, `cooldown`                                                          |
| retention (auto claim 91 days later)                                  | sent tombstoned and `already_claimed` / `retired`; `claimed` and `unknown` kept            |
| real poll: one DM, lost result, restart                               | 1 POST (exact text body), `sent`; later polls `skipped` / `already_claimed`                |
| overlapping polls + internal manual claim of a second event           | 1 POST; manual effect stays `claimed`, never sent by the poll                              |
| takeover before poll; takeover during the POST; next turn; stale resume | `skipped`/`takeover`, 0 POST; POST completes `sent` with `inFlight` reported; next turn `takeover`; `conflict` |
| foreign recipient; success + error envelope; then repeats             | `unknown` each, never re-POSTed (2 POSTs for 2 events)                                     |
| reconnect to another account (`/me` = ME2)                            | reads/POSTs as ME2, effect in `instagram-dm\|ME2`; ME's effect untouched                   |
| missing binding                                                       | `not_configured` / `dm-claim-store`, 0 DM POST                                             |
| restart: crash before claim / storage fails at claim                  | none → 1 POST after restart, `sent`                                                        |
| restart: POST in flight / provider answered, no receipt / receipt fails | `claimed` survives; 0 further POST; later polls `already_claimed`                       |
| restart: after receipt commit                                         | `sent`; 0 further POST                                                                     |

**Budget.** Per DM: 1 external POST + 2 internal coordinator calls (claim, settle), all three reserved from
`REPLIES_FETCH_BUDGET` (30, unchanged) before the claim, + 3 KV reads (fence). Per DM tick: 1 external GET `/me`
(0 when the poll fetched `/me` that tick) + 1 KV read (status). Worst case DM side at `REPLY_CAP` 8: external 10 (`/me`,
conversations, 8 POSTs), internal 16, KV reads 25. Whole tick: at most 30 budgeted outbound + DM coordinator calls,
plus the public branch's pre-existing unbudgeted coordinator calls (at most 16, comments and DMs share the cap): ≤ 46.
