**Design per finding (`store/index.ts`, `lib/cloudWorkflowJournal.ts`):**
- 7C2A-1: `journalSafeStorage` is replaced by `serializedStorage` (same key, same lock, no schema).
  - An ordinary save sets `savePending` and queues one lock task (`saveQueued`). Several saves coalesce into that one
    task.
  - Inside the hold, `runPendingSave()` reads storage fresh. It takes the journal slice from storage verbatim: an
    absent slice stays absent, and the write is refused unless the raw text contains `"cloudJournal":` followed by the
    canonical slice, so the bytes written are the stored bytes. It writes the latest `pickLocal(memory)`.
  - `articlesLock()` flushes a pending save synchronously at the start of every hold, so there is never a recursive
    acquisition and a commit's rehydrate cannot drop the save.
  - Locked writers mark their own synchronous writes with `writeHeld("journal" | "keep" | "memory")`. Journal commits,
    reset and restore author the journal; other `commitFresh` commits keep the stored bytes.
  - Without Web Locks the save runs at once, still with the stored bytes.
  - `hydrateStore` and the storage/pageshow listeners do not rehydrate while a save is pending.
  - New exports: `saveStatus` and `savesSettled()`.
- 7C2A-2: `storedPayload()` returns one of three kinds:
  - none: no save yet.
  - ok: an object root with an object `state`; a legacy save without the journal is allowed.
  - unreadable: a throwing read, non-JSON, `null`, an array, a string, or a missing or non-object `state`.

  `durableJournal()` uses it, so an invalid outer shape now loads as `journal-unreadable`. Ordinary saves and restores
  refuse on unreadable storage without writing. Settings shows `settings.saveFailed` (`role="alert"`, EN/AR) while
  `saveStatus.failed` is set.
- 7C2A-3: `compareObservations` compares `proofOf` (the observation with `binding.kind` nulled), so the identical
  authority, binding identity and full receipt seen via any request kind is `same`. Callers keep the first stored
  observation. Ack enrichment and real contradictions are unchanged.
- 7C2A-4:
  - Restore rehydrates inside the lock before building `before`; the path without a lock stays one synchronous step.
  - The rollback journal is the stored slice.
  - `rollBack(epoch, before)` (restore and reset) writes `before` back only when storage holds the operation's epoch.
    Otherwise it writes nothing: memory goes back to `before` and rehydrates. The candidate library is replaced only on
    success.

**Journal design** (`lib/cloudWorkflowJournal.ts`, pure; `store/index.ts`, additive):
- Schema `{v:1, generation, commitId, suppression:{epoch, resetAt, commitId}, entries[]}`; entry `{key, authority:{origin,
  ownerKey}, occurrenceId, body, payloadDigest, executionAt, commitId, state: queued|suppressed, observation|null}`. Key =
  the protocol's `occurrenceKey` (canonical JSON array). `parseJournal` is strict (exact keys at every level, key
  re-derived from the canonical authority, body = Worker `checkBody` at its own executionAt with owner/occurrence/
  executionAt bound, state = derived from suppression, unique keys, <= 600); `verifyJournal` recomputes every body digest
  (mismatch = unreadable) and revalidates every observation.
- Observation `{authority, binding:{kind, ownerKey, occurrenceId, payloadDigest}, receipt}` (full receipt as JSON). Live
  ingest needs a parser-branded receipt (`isVerifiedReceipt`) from a submit/status-row/cancel/run `Parsed` whose request
  matches; a compact feed is `compact-feed`, a look-alike `unverified`. Persisted/imported observations are accepted only if
  the pinned `parseAnswer` re-parses them now as a status row for the entry's authority with `expect` = the entry's body
  and digest (no cast, no stored flag; a stored `verified` key is a structural failure). Ordering: higher receipt version
  newer; equal version must match except the ack fields, where an acknowledged receipt only adds; otherwise conflict.
  The projection (`loadCloudJournal`) returns plain data (`observed:{state, receiptVersion}`, `observationRejected`);
  no branded receipt, delivered or ackable marker leaves it. No ack/adoption API.
- CAS/read-back path reused: `commitFresh` (shared `3z-prod-articles` Web Lock, fresh rehydration, write, exact canonical
  read-back of the whole journal, rollback). One additive optional `newer` hook: after a failed read-back, if storage holds
  another readable journal at/after the proposed generation, memory reloads instead of writing the rollback over it.
  Validation/detach/hash and observation revalidation run before the lock; the enqueue base (suppression epoch) is
  captured before validation (a reset/restore meanwhile = `stale`); observe CASes on the validated entry digest and
  observation. No network under the lock.
- Typed failures: `unsupported-save` (no Web Locks), `not-persisted` (lock error, blocked/quota storage, failed read-back),
  `journal-unreadable` (malformed stored journal: never treated as empty; the slice is opaque `z.unknown()` in the
  persisted schema so other slices stay readable and the raw journal is kept verbatim by other writes), `invalid`,
  `too-large` (8 KiB context / 16 KiB body), `limitation` (4,000-unit cloud output: action, built prefix, skipped
  suffix), `suppressed`, `stale`, `capacity`, `conflict` (with current), observe: `missing`, `older`, `conflict`,
  `observation-unverified`.
- Cap 600: update of an existing entry allowed at the cap, new entry refused, overflowing import refused before any write;
  no eviction or retirement.
- Suppression: reset advances `{epoch+1, resetAt = max(previous, now), commitId}` under the lock with the journal kept and
  every state re-derived from immutable executionAt. Import merge against the fresh durable journal: union of entries at
  their original authority and commit token, monotonic observations, max epoch and max resetAt independently (marker
  commitId kept when one side dominates, new otherwise), contradictions refuse the whole restore (`journal-conflict`
  with keys), revalidation failures `journal-invalid`, legacy backup (no slice) keeps the device journal, Inbox-control
  restore merge/read-back unchanged.
- Reset result: `reset(now?) => Promise<{ok:true, retained} | {ok:false, reason:"not-persisted"|"journal-unreadable"}>`;
  one write (ordinary content cleared, journal kept) proven by the journal read-back and the new library epoch; a failure
  rolls back (never over a newer journal) and replaces no candidate library. Runs under the lock after a fresh
  rehydration; at once only where nothing can race: no Web Locks (as the accepted restore), no browser (memory-only), or
  no save yet. No synchronous bypass that can erase a durable journal.

1. **Monotonic journal on ordinary saves.** The persist storage is now `journalSafeStorage(createJSONStorage(...))`: every
   write of the store key (ordinary saves, commitFresh patches, reset, restore, rollback) reads the stored payload and
   writes `journalForSave(stored, incoming)` instead of the incoming slice. `journalForSave` reuses `mergeJournals`
   (new optional `keep-fresh` mode: a same-key digest difference or an equal-version contradiction keeps the stored
   entry instead of refusing): every stored entry kept, higher receipt version wins, max epoch and max resetAt
   independently; an unreadable stored journal is returned unchanged (left for the locked path); a stored journal
   that already holds everything is written back byte for byte; an incoming journal that already holds everything
   (locked commits, reset, restore) is written verbatim, so the locked CAS/read-back and reset's suppression advance are
   unchanged; otherwise the union one generation past both. Over capacity keeps the stored journal whole. Ceiling: a
   payload that is not JSON at all is still overwritten by an ordinary save (no slice exists to keep; an existing pinned
   test, `store/index.test.ts` R1-C, repairs such a payload with an ordinary save).
2. **No Web Locks = no journal write.** `importState` with a journal slice and no lock resolves
   `{ok:false, reason:"unsupported-save"}` before validation or any write; a backup without the slice still restores
   at once and leaves the stored slice exactly as it is (it no longer writes an empty journal either). `reset` without
   the lock refuses `unsupported-save` (no write) when the durable journal has entries; with no entries it clears
   content and writes no journal (stored slice left untouched, no suppression advance). A reset on a device with no save
   now also writes no journal (there is none to keep). Settings maps `unsupported-save` to the not-saved copy (reset and
   restore). `ResetResult`/`ImportStateResult` gain `unsupported-save`.
3. Consequence for the earlier test adaptations: with the empty-device reset writing no journal, four of the five
   whole-state equality sites in `store/index.test.ts` (683, 1657, 1682, 2052) are back to their ORIGINAL assertion
   unchanged; only the articles round trip keeps `expectSameExceptJournal` (it resets under a lock with a save, so the
   marker advances), now tolerant of a pre-reset backup without a journal. The eight mechanical awaits stay. My own
   store-journal tests changed their expected epochs (2 to 1) and simulate a second device with an empty reset; the
   two-enqueue race test now accepts either winner (it flipped once under full load: assertion order, not behaviour).

**Before editing.** The three code files copied to `base/workers/scout/src/social/` and the README to
`base/workers/scout/`; sha256 matched the scope (`workflowCoordinator.ts 35f5a116…`, test `42e5e5f6…`,
`workflowRun.runtime.test.ts 4854dfbe…`, README `d9bf24e2…`).

**Approach.** Smallest correct diff at the shared point: in `commitStep`'s commit transaction and in `finish`, a
`stamp = Math.max(now, Number(r.updated_at))` is computed from the row read inside the same synchronous transaction
as the existing receiptVersion/digest CAS, and replaces `now` for step `at`, output `created_at`, `started_at`
(COALESCE), `updated_at` and `finished_at`. `updated_at` already bounds `started_at` and every step time, so
nondecreasing times follow. The run loop and a finish-only retry (and the public `finish`/`commitStep` ops) all route
through it; `run` needed no change but its doc comment. Equal times allowed; no +1 ms, outside clock, endpoint, state,

**Deviations / concerns.**
1. *Over-bound builder records* — the real builder can emit a record the existing allowlist refuses on a bound, not a
   field (e.g. a 500-character template of `{summary}` × 3 over a 2,000-character summary → 6,000-character idea text
   > `OUTPUT_TEXT_MAX` 4,000). Unhandled, commitStep would answer `bad_request` and the occurrence could never progress;
   the adapter maps it to the existing `invalid` step error (fail-fast, nothing stored, never truncated, allowlist not
   widened). The app's local executor would keep such a record; the cloud run fails that step instead. Needs a ruling
   if the planner prefers a different code or an admission-time bound.
2. *Row 28 scheduled half* — admission (pinned protocol) refuses a context of another week, so `context-stale` is only
   reachable through the adapter directly (proven in Node), not end-to-end; it stays a DT-7D fixture.
3. *Restart-between-steps fixtures* commit the earlier step(s) with the host-computed real-builder record (a crash
   between steps cannot be triggered from a request, and no step-count parameter is allowed); the steps after the
   restart are built in workerd by the adapter and the whole set is byte-equal to the host.
4. *Contention evidence* — the unit test injects a genuine concurrent writer (a real `commitStep` of the same step by
   another caller while the run awaits an output digest, via a spy on `crypto.subtle.digest`); workerd shows real
   concurrent runs (commits sum 5) but exhaustion of the budget is proven in the unit suite only.
5. `limit` is unreachable with `ACTIONS_MAX = 5` (finish precedes it); kept as the documented bound and route rule.
6. The run route refuses any query string (`?…` → 400), stricter than the other POST routes, so no parameter can act
   as a toggle.
7. Bundle grows by ~0.95 MB raw / ~190 KB gzip (690,828 B gzip total), within Workers limits but worth watching.
8. Purge maintenance, DT-7C browser proof/reset/import, DT-7D schedule, DT-7E activity and live readiness remain open.

  `ackedVersion ∈ {0, receiptVersion}`, `firstAckAt` iff acknowledged); the step table below with the body's actions;
  one output per done step, linked, `validOutput`, record digest recomputed. Any throw = not proof.
- *Feed item:* exact keys, unique occurrenceId in the page, ≤ 5 steps, the same step table without a body (unique
  action ids, supported kinds), outputs only on terminal items, `validDraft` + recomputed digests; the compact wire
  shape and `nextAfter`/`more` rule unchanged. No body/target binding is claimed.
- *Mutation success* and *refusals:* the tables below. Every failure → `503 receipt_unavailable`, nothing echoed, no
  further coordinator call (tests assert exactly one call).

Derived state/step table (from `submit`/`commitStep`/`finish`/`cancel`; letters p d f s = pending, done, failed,
skipped; version = 1 at submit, +1 per committed step incl. its fail-fast skip, +1 at finish/cancel):

| state | step pattern | receiptVersion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pending | `p+` | 1 |
| running | `d+p+` \| `d+` (all done, before finish) \| `d*fs*` (fail-fast, before finish) | 1 + done + failed |
| done | `d+` | done + 2 |
| partial | `d+fs*` | done + 3 |
| failed | `fs*` | 3 |
| cancelled | `s+` (no outputs, no startedAt) | 2 |

Step fields: done = `outputId wf:<occ>:<action>`, `outputDigest`, `at`, no error; failed = error ∈ builder errors ∪
`output-conflict`, `at`, no output fields; pending/skipped = none of them.

Mutation binding (code semantics win): register (created true|false) = requested workflow, epoch `expectedEpoch + 1`,
revision, digest, active, all earlier epochs closed; created:true also needs the new epoch's `openedAt = updatedAt`.
Update = requested epoch, revision, digest, active; changed:true also needs `revision > expectedRevision`
(changed:false is the code's replay at the same revision+digest whatever `expectedRevision`). Pause/resume = requested
epoch, `revision = expectedRevision`, `paused` = the verb (state not bound: the code controls an unregistered current
epoch too). Unregister = requested epoch, `revision = expectedRevision`, `unregistered`, epoch closed; changed:true needs
`closedAt = updatedAt`. Cancel: true ⇒ a valid cancelled receipt; false ⇒ a valid terminal receipt (the code answers
running with a refusal). Ack: as before plus `ackedVersion ∈ {0, receiptVersion}`, `firstAckAt` iff `ackedVersion ≥ 1`,
`purgeAt ≤ firstAckAt + 90 d`. Submit: created:true ⇒ fresh pending receipt (version 1). Registrations everywhere:
≤ 50 epochs; every earlier epoch closed; the current one closed exactly when unregistered.

Refusal table (allowed errors per operation, from the coordinator): submit = bad_request, unsupported_id, too_large,
authority_mismatch, digest_mismatch, pruned, conflict{occurrenceId}, not_registered, unknown_epoch,
registration_behind, capacity; register = bad_request, authority_mismatch, conflict{registration}, capacity;
update/pause/resume/unregister = bad_request, authority_mismatch, not_registered, conflict{registration}; status and
changes = bad_request, authority_mismatch; cancel = bad_request, authority_mismatch, pruned, absent, running; ack =
bad_request, authority_mismatch, pruned, absent, not_terminal, future_version. Extras typed: ids = the request's,
`payloadDigest` digest, `prunedAt` ISO, `receiptVersion` ≥ 1, not_terminal state pending (version 1) | running (≥ 2),
future_version only above the requested version, `registration` null only for register with `expectedEpoch ≠ 0`, else
a valid registration that is not the request's own success (register: not the replay, not a re-registrable row;
update: not the replay, not an applicable CAS; control: not epoch+revision matching). Pure errors and the ownerKey
binding unchanged.

Binding decisions (recorded before implementation):
1. **Ack/retention.** Only the exact current terminal receipt version acknowledges; a future version is rejected; a
   stale/lower one is a no-op with no new proof; nonterminal/absent/pruned get explicit replies and no ack.
   `firstAckAt` is persisted on the first valid terminal ack (Worker clock) and never moved. Purge deadline:
   acknowledged = `min(finishedAt + 180 d, firstAckAt + 90 d)`; unacknowledged = `finishedAt + 180 d`; nonterminal never
   purged; permanent tombstones; ack does not bump the change feed (no echo loop).
2. **Pause/resume.** Workflow-level pause (the current registration row's `state`, keyed by `workflowId`, governing all
   epochs incl. delayed old-epoch work) blocks the first pending→running step inside that same transaction; paused
   submit stays pending; resume enables it; running pure occurrences finish; unregister neither moves cloud work to local
   nor cancels it; no replaced snapshot lookup can change an occurrence body.
3. **Failure policy.** Fail-fast: a stale planner context fails that plan step and skips all later steps; earlier
   outputs survive; `partial` only if an earlier step succeeded, else `failed` (`[idea, stale plan, post]` keeps the idea
   and skips the post; `[stale plan, idea]` produces no idea). Design matrix row 28 corrected before coding. No scheduler.
4. **Authority/CAS.** One fixed server-selected Durable Object name for this single-owner dashboard (never from caller
   ownerKey/bearer). `ownerKey` generated once in durable `meta`, stable across restarts/deploys. CAS binds
   `registrationEpoch` + `revision`. Closed-epoch cutoff metadata retained (pre- vs post-unregister admission); unknown
   epochs refused; register/re-register idempotent on retry (no second epoch from a lost answer).
5. **Exact bodies.** The server recomputes the payload digest from the canonical allowlisted body (digest field
   excluded), with published deterministic test vectors; an asserted digest over different content is refused. Bounded
   collections/text, unique action ids, supported ids, body authority, trigger/input/context/target-week consistency,
   valid timestamps; the accepted body and `executionAt` are kept exactly. A step requires the next pending index and
   all prior prerequisites; finish refuses with pending steps. Real atomic SQLite transactions; immutable tuple/digest
   adoption; monotonic versions and sequences; any async digest work outside the transaction, rechecked inside.
6. **Feed/status.** Latest-receipt change feed (may coalesce); every relevant transition gets a durable sequence;
   bounded pages with a precise `nextAfter`/`more` rule; full status = ownerKey, occurrenceId, immutable body incl.
   executionAt, payload digest, receiptVersion, typed step/output proof; absent/pruned/error distinguishable and
   authority-bound; outputs are allowlisted drafts only; no caller-supplied output/builder/step through public routes.

  step 0, two resumes, stale executor.

- 7A-4: durable per-occurrence proof (`outputIds`, `deletedOutputIds`, `resetEpoch`) + persisted `workflowResetEpoch/
  resetAt`; import max/union; retirement only after Worker `pruned`; cap 600 with visible pause, never discard.
- 7A-5: exact projection for the occurrence's target week (completions `{skillId,quest,at}` before the week; that week's
  plan rows incl. `quest`, `by`, minutes-0 tombstones; gear/davinciEdition), ordered fold of earlier plan outputs,
  scheduled `context-stale` failure for plan steps.
- 7A-6: authority `{workerOrigin, ownerKey}` (non-secret server id), in-memory token fingerprint fences, imported/other-
  Worker outbox never retargeted, ids `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$` (no colon ⇒ no `wf:` tuple collision; DT-5 format kept),
  same-id/changed-digest `409 conflict`, opt-in/unregister never transfers an occurrence to local.
- 7A-7: schedule declaration on the 5-minute grid, initial watermark at registration, ≤ 3 admitted + one `missed`
  interval per call in one transaction, rollback on interruption, capacity keeps the watermark, pause span = one interval.
- 7A-8: field-specific labels (successful sync / last saved check / data freshness / last saved result + status / job

**Planner summary (~600 words).**
- *Today:* workflows run only in an open browser tab (DT-4): `newRun` snapshots the workflow + input; `drainStep`
  builds one output per `commitFresh` under the `3z-prod-articles` lock with id `wf:<runId>:<actionId>`, adopting an
  existing id; the Ready transition enqueues runs in the same commit; `RUNS_MAX = 200`. DT-5 maps a workflow post id to
  `j-…-<sha256[0:24]>` via `publishJobId`/`jobOwnership` — preserved verbatim.
- *Registration & privacy:* cloud execution is opt-in per workflow; each occurrence's executor (`local`/`cloud`) is
  fixed at creation. A registration holds the workflow snapshot (`id, name, trigger, actions, revision`) plus an
  allowlisted planner projection (skills in use, gear, DaVinci edition, lang, current-week plan rows and the completions
  `buildWeekPlan` needs) — never articles beyond the trigger, idea/post banks, inbox, tokens or business kit.
- *Occurrence identity:* manual = browser `newId()` persisted before the request; article-ready = `ar:` +
  sha256(workflowId|articleId|readyCommitId); scheduled = `sc:` + sha256(workflowId|nominal slot). A browser outbox is
  written in the same commit as Ready/Run now; Riyadh day is captured at creation; missed scheduled slots: newest 3
  materialized, older recorded `missed`; revision changes never replay history.
- *Atomicity:* one SQLite `WorkflowCoordinator` per account: insert-if-absent occurrences, `UPDATE … WHERE
  state='pending' RETURNING` claim, one transaction per step (output row + step + `receipt_version`), adopt existing
  output on resume, pause holds claims, cancel only `pending`, retention 90 days after ack / 180 absolute with permanent
  tombstones, 500 live cap with refusal (never eviction). Steps are pure drafts (posts `stage: idea`); no publish job,
  provider call or message from the cloud in DT-7.
- *Browser reconciliation:* per occurrence, insert outputs only if the id is absent and not locally tombstoned (dirty
  edits kept, deletes never resurrected), record the run receipt, read back, then ack monotonic `receiptVersion`.
  Import probes before re-delivering outbox entries; reset is fenced by `articlesGen`; tabs serialize on the one lock;
  proof never depends on the 200-run history list. DT-5 cross-tab cancel/resync limit unchanged (no cloud publish jobs).
- *Activity:* shows only stored facts — sync `lastSyncAt`, replies `lastPollAt/lockUntil`, publish job states,
  trend/effects/category `updatedAt`/`attempts` — labelled "last success at"/"observed at", next eligible slot from
  `cron.ts` in Riyadh time, `unknown` where nothing proves a state; per-tick history needs later instrumentation; cron
  budgets unchanged.
- *First slice (DT-7B):* Worker-only `workflowCoordinator.ts` + `workflowRoutes.ts` (+ pure executor only if
  `lib/workflows.ts` compiles in the Worker without app deps; else stop and record), narrow wiring (`routes.ts`,
  `store.ts` env field, fifth `index.ts` export, additive local migration `v5-workflows`), unit + workerd runtime tests
  for matrix rows 1–17, 25–28. Browser outbox/reconciliation (DT-7C), cron materialization (DT-7D), activity view (DT-7E)
  and publication (DT-8) follow separately.
- *Activation prerequisites (unchanged):* active Cloudflare identity/traffic, applied bindings/migrations, secret
  presence, minimal legacy delivery/cooldown inventory, reviewed automatic-reply cutover, actual provider grants and
  version/window support. DT-6 is locally built/tested, not live-ready; TikTok Inbox and DT-8–DT-10 remain open.

No build, tests, server, restart, remote read, Cloudflare probe, provider/Worker/control call, grant, secret,
provisioning, migration, workflow dispatch, billing, push/merge/deploy or gate change. Codex evidence and review files
